chunks.title: Fortnox OSS Configuration Guide
chunks.text: Path: Settings → Accounting → VAT Codes → Create New

chunks.title: Fortnox OSS Configuration Guide
chunks.text: Create one VAT code for each EU country you sell to.

chunks.title: Fortnox OSS Configuration Guide
chunks.text: Fortnox names the VAT code automatically — you only set the VAT rate.

chunks.title: Fortnox OSS Configuration Guide
chunks.text: Create a separate VAT code per country, even if two countries share the same rate (e.g. Denmark and Croatia are both 25%, but need different codes).

chunks.title: Fortnox OSS Configuration Guide
chunks.text: Example reference: VAT Code · VAT Rate · Country

chunks.title: Connections
chunks.text: The Connections page shows every application linked to Lighthouse as part of your integration setup. Each connection is the authenticated bridge that allows Lighthouse to send and receive data between your systems.

chunks.title: Connections
chunks.text: Connections are set up by the Cloudify team during onboarding. You do not need to configure them manually — this page is for viewing status and managing existing connections.

chunks.title: Connections

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Reliable webhook management — route, filter, transform, and deliver payloads from any trigger to one or multiple targets.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Lighthouse Flows is your webhook management layer inside Lighthouse. It receives incoming webhook payloads, applies filtering and transformation rules, and delivers the data reliably to one or more target endpoints.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Lighthouse Flows handles webhook routing and delivery. It is separate from your integration workflows — Flows focuses on where data goes and how it gets there, not on the business logic that transforms it.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: *** How It Works Every Flow is built on three layers that work in sequence.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Receives the incoming webhook payload. Validates the signature and accepts the event into the Flow.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Applies your rules — filter which payloads pass through, transform the data shape, and configure retry and rate-limiting behaviour.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Delivers the processed payload to one or more HTTP endpoints — securely and reliably.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: *** Triggers The Trigger layer is where your Flow begins. It listens for incoming webhook events and validates them before they enter the pipeline.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Accepts real-time data through webhook inputs. Any system that can send an HTTP POST can act as a trigger source.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Verifies the authenticity of each incoming payload — ensuring only legitimate events enter your Flow.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Supports webhook, polling, and schedule trigger types to match different source systems and use cases.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Add custom headers to your trigger configuration for source systems that require specific authentication or metadata fields.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: *** Flows The Flow layer sits between your trigger and your targets. This is where you control what data passes through, how it's shaped, and how delivery failures are handled.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Use Google's CEL (Common Expression Language) to write filter conditions — only payloads that match your rules are passed to the target. Irrelevant events are dropped before delivery.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Modify payloads before they reach the target — add calculated fields, reformat values, or restructure the JSON shape to match what your target expects.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Configure how failed deliveries are retried. Choose between linear back-off (fixed intervals) or exponential back-off (increasing intervals) to handle temporary target unavailability.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Cap the delivery rate to protect downstream systems from overload. Set limits per second, minute, hour, or day to match your target's capacity.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: *** Targets The Target layer defines where your processed payload is delivered. You can route a single trigger to multiple targets simultaneously.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Configure any HTTP endpoint as a delivery target. Supports standard REST endpoints that accept POST requests.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Send the same payload to multiple targets from a single trigger — useful when the same event needs to reach more than one system.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: All payloads are delivered over encrypted connections. Data in transit is protected from origin to destination.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Lighthouse Flows captures and processes responses from your target endpoints, giving you visibility into delivery outcomes.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Workflows execute your integration business logic — they read data from a source app, transform it, and write it to a destination app (e.g. HubSpot deal → Xero invoice).

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Flows handle webhook routing and delivery. They receive a raw webhook payload, apply filtering and transformation rules, and deliver it to HTTP targets — without executing integration logic. Use Flows when you need to fan-out, filter, or reliably relay webhook events between systems.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: CEL (Common Expression Language) is an open-source expression language developed by Google. In Lighthouse Flows, you write CEL expressions to define which incoming payloads should pass through to the target. Contact Cloudify if you need help writing filter expressions for your use case.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Lighthouse Flows retries the delivery according to the retry strategy configured in your Flow — either linear or exponential back-off. If all retries are exhausted, the delivery failure is logged and visible in Events History.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Yes. A single Flow can have multiple targets configured. The same payload — after filtering and transformation — is delivered to all targets.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Navigate to Flows in the Lighthouse sidebar. Click Get Started or New Flow to begin configuration. You will need to define your Trigger, configure any Flow rules, and add at least one Target. Contact Cloudify if you need assistance setting up your first Flow.

chunks.title: Lighthouse Flows
chunks.text: Lighthouse Flows supports three trigger types: Webhook (real-time push from an external system), Polling (Lighthouse pulls data from an external API on a schedule), and Schedule (a time-based trigger using AWS EventBridge rate or cron expressions).

chunks.title: Flows Events
chunks.text: *** Event Status Reference Status · Meaning · What To Do

chunks.title: Flows Events
chunks.text: successful · The event was delivered to all targets without error · No action needed

chunks.title: Flows Events
chunks.text: failed · All delivery attempts were exhausted — the event could not be delivered · Contact Cloudify with the Event ID and Latest Attempt ID

chunks.title: Flows Events
chunks.text: filtered · A CEL filter rule in the Flow blocked this event from delivery — this is intentional · Review your Flow's filter rules if this was unexpected

chunks.title: Flows Events
chunks.text: pending · The event is queued and waiting for its next delivery attempt · No action needed — it will process automatically

chunks.title: Flows Events
chunks.text: Filter by Status → failed to immediately surface all events that exhausted retries and need attention.

chunks.title: Flows Events
chunks.text: A filtered status is not an error. It means an event was intentionally stopped by a rule configured in the Flow. Contact Cloudify if you are seeing unexpected filtered results.

chunks.title: Prerequistes
chunks.text: This document outlines the essential prerequisites for successfully integrating HubSpot and e-conomic. Adhering to these requirements will ensure a smooth integration process, optimal data synchronization, and secure operation.

chunks.title: Prerequistes
chunks.text: Before beginning the integration process, please ensure you have:

chunks.title: Prerequistes
chunks.text: An active HubSpot account with administrative access

chunks.title: Prerequistes
chunks.text: An active e-conomic account with administrative access

chunks.title: Prerequistes
chunks.text: Necessary authentication credentials for both platforms

chunks.title: Connect Visma e-conomic
chunks.text: Installation process Log in to your HubSpot account and search for the ‘Visma e-conomic’ app in HubSpot Marketplace. If you have already logged in to your Hubspot account, visit the application link directly.

chunks.title: Connect Visma e-conomic
chunks.text: Click Install app. Select the account you want to use to install the e-conomic app and click ‘Choose account’.

chunks.title: Connect Visma e-conomic
chunks.text: Mark the tick option and click "Connect App".

chunks.title: Connect Visma e-conomic
chunks.text: Click on “Connect” to connect your e-conomic account.

chunks.title: Connect Visma e-conomic
chunks.text: You will be asked to input your e-conomic credentials. First, fill in the email ID connected to your e-conomic account. Click "Next".

chunks.title: Connect Visma e-conomic
chunks.text: Permission will be asked from you to add the app to your agreement. Click "Add App".

chunks.title: Connect Visma e-conomic
chunks.text: Once you have connected your e-conomic account, you will be automatically redirected to the final step.

chunks.title: Connect Visma e-conomic
chunks.text: Click on “Yes, setup automation” or “I’ll do it manually” to proceed. Choose the option that best fits your workflow.

chunks.title: Set Up Customer Matching
chunks.text: To begin customizing your customer mappings and preferences, click on the “Customize” button.

chunks.title: Set Up Customer Matching
chunks.text: Company Matching Criteria (For Business Customers - B2B)

chunks.title: Set Up Customer Matching
chunks.text: You can configure company matching criteria by selecting a field in HubSpot (e.g., Company Name, Email) corresponding to the chosen e-conomic field. This ensures both platforms refer to the same company data when syncing information, maintaining consistency across systems.

chunks.title: Set Up Customer Matching
chunks.text: Enable Individual Contact Sync (For Individual Customers - B2C)

chunks.title: Set Up Customer Matching
chunks.text: Note: Enable this only if you deal with individual contacts as well

chunks.title: Set Up Customer Matching
chunks.text: This feature is essential for businesses dealing directly with consumers. It allows the seamless addition of individual contacts from HubSpot to e-conomic as customers when there's no associated company. Therefore, if this is the case, tick “Enable individual customer sync”.

chunks.title: Set Up Customer Matching
chunks.text: Once you have selected your preferences, click on the "Next" button.

chunks.title: One-click Invoice/Quote/Order
chunks.text: The Visma e-conomic integration by Cloudify facilitates one-click creation of invoices, quotes or orders directly from HubSpot deals, irrespective of the deal stage.

chunks.title: One-click Invoice/Quote/Order
chunks.text: Selecting I'll do it manually skips automation and takes you to the Cloudify Dashboard, allowing you to update invoices from any HubSpot deal stage.

chunks.title: One-click Invoice/Quote/Order
chunks.text: Once you click Dashboard, follow these steps to complete a manual sync:

chunks.title: One-click Invoice/Quote/Order
chunks.text: Go to any invoice on the dashboard you wish to update and click Review and Sync. The manual sync window will immediately appear on your screen.

chunks.title: One-click Invoice/Quote/Order
chunks.text: Ensure customer, currency, layout, and delivery details are correctly selected

chunks.title: One-click Invoice/Quote/Order
chunks.text: Review and update date, payment terms, delivery info, references, and line items, then choose the appropriate action (Invoice, Quote, or Order) to proceed

chunks.title: One-click Invoice/Quote/Order
chunks.text: Add new products using the “Add Line Item” button to select from e-conomic or modify existing ones by deleting or cloning. You can also apply discounts for a customized and final invoice, order quote.

chunks.title: One-click Invoice/Quote/Order
chunks.text: Click the three-dots menu to Split your invoice by percentage or Duplicate it.

chunks.title: One-click Invoice/Quote/Order
chunks.text: Click Sync to push the draft to e-conomic. You can view the final invoice in the deal's attachments or notes.

chunks.title: Set Up Product Matching
chunks.text: Product Search Rules define how products from HubSpot are matched with those in e-conomic, enabling a simple field-based matching or a direct connection without searching to ensure accurate product syncing and invoicing.

chunks.title: Set Up Product Matching
chunks.text: Simple Search This feature is used to match products between HubSpot and e-conomic by correlating a specific field, such as SKU or product number. It's particularly useful for users who have long product lists. Choose the corresponding field in HubSpot and e-conomic for automatic identification from the respective dropdowns.

chunks.title: Set Up Product Matching
chunks.text: Direct Link ﻿Select this method to link specific products one-to-one between HubSpot and e-conomic directly. This option is particularly beneficial when the product count is low, allowing for precise, manual matching of each product.

chunks.title: Set Up Product Matching
chunks.text: Advance Settings Set Product Matching Fallback Options

chunks.title: Set Up Product Matching
chunks.text: This option is useful when a product is not found in the search. It offers three options, which are:

chunks.title: Set Up Product Matching
chunks.text: Skip Invoice Generation: Select this option if you prefer not to create an invoice when a product isn't found in e-conomic

chunks.title: Set Up Product Matching
chunks.text: Use a Default product: When an item is not found in e-conomic, a default item from e-conomic will be used to generate the invoice. If you select this option, you must specify a default product from your e-conomic item list.

chunks.title: Set Up Product Matching
chunks.text: Create a new product in e-conomic : This option automatically generates a new item entry in e-conomic when a matching item isn't found using product details from HubSpot.

chunks.title: Set Up Product Matching
chunks.text: Sync deals which do not have line-items (products) associated with them

chunks.title: Set Up Product Matching
chunks.text: This additional option is provided to create an invoice, order/quote with deal value only. You can choose this option if you do not use line items in HubSpot deals. Select a default product from the list to handle this scenario. Click on "Save customization" once done.

chunks.title: Set Up Invoice/Order/Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Specify how invoices, orders or quotes are generated in e-conomic by linking them to your HubSpot sales flow.

chunks.title: Set Up Invoice/Order/Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Select a Pipeline from the drop-down menu. This step allows you to link the creation of invoices or quotes to a specific sales pipeline in HubSpot. It ensures that the invoices or quotes are generated at the right time in the sales process, improving efficiency and reducing the risk of errors associated with manual entry.

chunks.title: Set Up Invoice/Order/Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Note: Feel free to click "Get Guided Installation" if you require assistance from Cloudify experts regarding the installation steps.

chunks.title: Set Up Invoice/Order/Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Select the Deal Stage from the drop-down menu. Here, you select the particular stage within the sales pipeline that will trigger the creation of an invoice, order or quotes in e-conomic. This ensures the invoicing process aligns perfectly with your established sales flow.

chunks.title: Set Up Invoice/Order/Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Choose the Invoice, Order/ Quote from the next drop-down menu. This action involves creating a draft invoice,order/quote as per your requirement.

chunks.title: Set Up Invoice/Order/Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: After selecting the required options, click on "Add Pipeline".

chunks.title: Set Up Invoice/Order/Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Once you’ve added the pipeline, you can click on “Customize” to set up your Customer Matching and Product Matching preferences, or click on “Complete Setup” to directly view the dashboard and start syncing.

chunks.title: Set Up Invoice/Order/Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Note: You can add more pipelines as per your requirements by clicking on Add Pipeline. Feel free to Get Guided Installation if you require assistance from Cloudify experts regarding the installation steps.

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Configure rate limiting, retry logic, and error handling in FlowLink to improve reliability and performance.

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Use these settings to control how FlowLink handles request volume, retries failed actions, and logs errors.

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Rate Limiting Set Max Requests per Second

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Use the Delivery Rate setting in your webhook configuration to control how many requests FlowLink can send per second. The source page gives the example that setting this value to 5 means FlowLink will send no more than 5 requests per second. :contentReference\[oaicite:1]

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Queue Management FlowLink automatically queues requests that exceed the configured rate limit and processes them in order as capacity becomes available. The page recommends starting with a conservative rate and increasing it gradually while monitoring performance. :contentReference\[oaicite:2]

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Start with a lower delivery rate first, then increase it gradually once you confirm the receiving system can handle the traffic reliably.

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Error Handling Configure Retry Logic When retry handling is enabled, you can define how FlowLink should retry failed requests using these settings. :contentReference\[oaicite:3]

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Retry Delay Set the initial wait time before the first retry attempt, in milliseconds. The source page gives 2000 ms (2 seconds) as an example. :contentReference\[oaicite:4]

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Retry Strategy Choose one of these retry strategies: :contentReference\[oaicite:5]

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Linear — consistent intervals between retry attempts

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Exponential — increasing intervals between retry attempts

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Example comparison using an initial delay of 2000 ms: :contentReference\[oaicite:6]

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Linear: retries at 2s, 4s, 6s, and 8s after the initial failure

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Exponential: retries at 2s, 6s, 14s, and 30s after the initial failure

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Max Attempts Set the maximum number of retry attempts before the action is marked as failed. The page’s example says that if this is set to 4, FlowLink will make the initial attempt plus 4 retries. :contentReference\[oaicite:7]

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Retry Delay, Retry Strategy, and Max Attempts settings in FlowLink

chunks.title: Performance Optimization
chunks.text: Error Logging FlowLink automatically logs errors in the HubSpot workflow history. The source page recommends reviewing these logs regularly so you can identify and address recurring issues. :contentReference\[oaicite:8]

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Customer Settings are the foundation of your integration, defining how customer information is matched, created, and updated between HubSpot and Fortnox. Proper configuration here ensures that your customer data remains consistent and accurate across both platforms.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Customer Matching Rules Customer Default Mappings

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Field Mappings *** Customer Matching Rules Why Customer Matching Rules Matter

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Prevent duplicate customers: By accurately matching HubSpot companies and contacts to existing Fortnox customers, you avoid creating duplicate records in Fortnox.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Ensure data consistency: Matching rules help maintain consistent customer data between HubSpot and Fortnox.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Streamline customer creation: When a match is not found, the app automatically creates a new customer in Fortnox.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Simplify customer management: Properly configured matching rules make it easier to manage your customer relationships across both platforms.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Customer Matching Rules Define Company Matching Criteria

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: In the "HubSpot" dropdown under "Company Matching Criteria", select the company property you want to use to identify the customer (e.g., CVR). In the "Fortnox" dropdown, select the corresponding customer field (e.g., Corporate Identification Num.).

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Customer Matching Rules Define Contact Matching Criteria (Optional)

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Check the box labelled "Enable Primary Contact Sync". In the "HubSpot" dropdown under "Contact Matching Criteria", select the contact property (e.g., Phone number). In the "Fortnox" dropdown, select the corresponding customer field (e.g., Phone Number).

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Customer Matching Rules Choose How to Handle the Customer Number

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Option 1 — Let Fortnox generate the customer number: Select "Let Fortnox create customer number" and choose whether to store the generated number in a HubSpot property.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Option 2 — Use a number from HubSpot: Select "Use customer number from HubSpot" and select the HubSpot property that contains the number you want to use.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Customer Matching Rules Review and Save Carefully review your settings to ensure they align with your business requirements. Click "Save" to apply your changes.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Why Customer Default Mappings Are Important

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Ensure all required Fortnox fields are filled: These mappings provide values for fields that Fortnox requires to create a new customer.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Streamline customer creation: By setting defaults, you reduce manual data entry and potential errors.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Maintain consistency: All new customers will have the same baseline settings unless overridden by HubSpot data.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Navigate to the Customer Default Mappings section in your integration settings.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: You'll see a list of required Fortnox fields: Payment Terms, Customer Group, VAT Zone, Currency, and Invoice Layout.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: For each field, click on the dropdown menu next to the field name and select the appropriate default value.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: After setting your preferred defaults for all required fields, click "Save" to apply your changes.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules

chunks.text: Why this happens: The connection with Fortnox has expired.

chunks.text: How to fix this: Open the Fortnox app from Connected Apps.

chunks.text: Navigate to Settings and click the Connect Fortnox button.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Product Not Present Why this happens: No line item or product is associated with the HubSpot deal. A line item is required to create an invoice in Fortnox, so the integration cannot proceed without one.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: How to fix this: You can either add a product to the deal in HubSpot, or configure a default Fortnox product to use as a fallback line item.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: To use a default Fortnox product (no deal product required):

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Open the Fortnox app from Connected Apps.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Navigate to General Settings → Sync Settings → Products.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Locate the "Do You Have Deals Without Products?" section and enable the checkbox.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Select a Fortnox product from the dropdown list.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Why this happens: A company is either not associated with the deal, or the app settings are not enabled to sync when only a contact is associated with the deal.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: How to fix this: If no Company or Contact is associated with the deal:

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Add a Company or Contact to the deal, then change the deal stage back and forth to re-trigger the integration.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: If only a Contact is associated with the deal (B2C):

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Navigate to General Settings → Sync Settings.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Under Customer Sync Rules, enable Contact (B2C) Sync.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot-Fortnox Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Set your preferred customer matching criteria between HubSpot Contact and Fortnox Customer.

chunks.text: if a match is found, the customer will be updated

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account

chunks.text: In the left menu, go to Company → Employees.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Why this happens: The connection with Xero has expired.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: How to fix this: Open the Xero Integration by Cloudify app from Connected Apps.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Navigate to Settings and click the Connect/Disconnect Xero button.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Why this happens: A company is either not associated with the deal, or the app settings are not enabled to sync when only a contact is associated with the deal.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: How to fix this: If no Company or Contact is associated with the deal:

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Add a Company or Contact to the deal, then change the deal stage back and forth to re-trigger the integration.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: If only a Contact is associated with the deal (B2C):

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Open the Xero Integration by Cloudify app from Connected Apps.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Under Customer Sync Rules, enable Contact (B2C) Sync.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Set your preferred customer matching criteria between HubSpot Contact and Xero Customer.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Account Not Valid Why this happens: The sales account mapped under customer default mappings is not suitable for revenue posting. The account must be of type Revenue in Xero.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Navigate to Settings → Customers → Customer Default Mappings.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Locate Default Sales Account and select the correct revenue-type account from the dropdown.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Product Not Present Why this happens: No line item or product is associated with the HubSpot deal. A line item is required to create an invoice in Xero, so the integration cannot proceed without one.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: How to fix this: You can either add a product to the deal in HubSpot, or configure a default Xero product to use as a fallback line item.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: To use a default Xero product (no deal product required):

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Locate the "Do You Have Deals Without Products?" section and enable the checkbox.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Select a Xero product from the dropdown list.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Why this happens: Xero only allows payments to be posted against accounts that have payments enabled in your Chart of Accounts. If the account used for this transaction doesn't have that setting turned on, Xero rejects the payment and the sync fails. Enabling payments for the relevant account resolves the error.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: How to fix this: In Xero, go to Settings → Chart of Accounts.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Select the account used to create the paid invoice in Xero.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Tick the Enable payments to this account checkbox and save.

chunks.title: Common HubSpot Xero errors and Fixes
chunks.text: Return to the HubSpot–Xero integration and rerun the failed sync. The invoice should now be created successfully.

chunks.title: Connect Xero Account

chunks.title: Connect Xero Account
chunks.text: Log in to your HubSpot account and search for Cloudify or Xero Integration app in the HubSpot Marketplace. This will display the Xero integration developed by Cloudify. Click Install app.

chunks.title: Connect Xero Account

chunks.title: Connect Xero Account

chunks.title: Connect Xero Account
chunks.text: On the next screen, select HubSpot and click Install.

chunks.title: Connect Xero Account
chunks.text: Once selected, you will be redirected to the HubSpot Marketplace login. Sign in and connect using the same steps mentioned in the From the HubSpot Marketplace tab above.

chunks.title: One Click Invoice/Quote
chunks.text: The HubSpot Xero integration by Cloudify facilitates one-click creation of invoices or quotes directly from HubSpot deals, irrespective of the deal stage.

chunks.text: Selecting I'll do it manually skips automation and takes you to the Cloudify Dashboard, allowing you to update invoices from any HubSpot deal stage.

chunks.text: Once you click Dashboard, follow these steps to complete a manual sync:

chunks.title: One Click Invoice/Quote

chunks.title: One Click Invoice/Quote

chunks.title: One Click Invoice/Quote

chunks.title: One Click Invoice/Quote

chunks.title: One Click Invoice/Quote

chunks.title: One Click Invoice/Quote

chunks.text: Lighthouse is Cloudify's integration platform — the engine that connects your apps, processes your data, and keeps everything running. This guide walks you through everything from creating your account to submitting your first integration request.

chunks.title: Getting Started with Lighthouse

chunks.title: Getting Started with Lighthouse
chunks.text: A clear window into your integrations — no technical expertise required.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Your integration health at a glance — run counts, success rates, and usage against your current plan.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The Overview page is your Lighthouse home base. Every time you log in, this is where you check the pulse of your integration — how many runs have processed, whether anything has failed, and how your usage compares to your plan.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: If your account is new and your integration hasn't processed any runs yet, all counters will show 0 and charts will display "Not enough data to show this graph." This is expected — the dashboard fills in as your workflows begin running.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: *** Plan Details The top-left panel shows your active subscription.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: When a plan is active, you'll see your plan name, the number of included runs, and your current billing cycle here.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: If this shows No Plan, your subscription hasn't been activated yet. Contact your Cloudify account manager to confirm your billing status before runs begin processing.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Your plan directly controls how many workflow runs Lighthouse will process each billing cycle. Always confirm your plan is active before going live.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: *** Usage Counters Two counters sit below the plan details and update in real time throughout your billing cycle.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Counter · What It Shows Runs Remaining · How many runs are left in your current plan allowance for this cycle

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Usage over Included · Runs that have exceeded your plan limit — if this is non-zero, review your plan

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: If Usage over Included shows a number greater than zero, you are processing more runs than your plan covers. Contact Cloudify to discuss upgrading your plan volume before your next billing cycle.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: *** Current Cycle The Current Cycle panel on the right shows a live breakdown of every run processed since your billing period started.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: All runs processed in this billing cycle — regardless of outcome.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Runs that completed successfully. This is your healthy baseline.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Runs that encountered an error. Go to Workflow Runs to investigate.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Runs currently in progress. Refresh the page to see them resolve.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Runs queued and waiting to start. These will process automatically.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Runs that were intentionally skipped based on your workflow logic.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: *** Today & This Week The same six counters — Total, Finished, Failed, Running, Pending, Skipped — are repeated for two shorter windows:

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Today — runs from the current calendar day

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: This Week — runs from the current calendar week

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Use Today and This Week for your daily check-in. Use Current Cycle to review overall health against your plan allowance.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: *** Performance Charts The lower half of the Overview page contains four charts that build up over time as your integration processes runs.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Chart · What It Shows Current cycle v/s Previous cycle · Side-by-side comparison of run volume between your current and last billing period

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Finished v/s Failed for Current cycle · The ratio of successful to failed runs in the current billing cycle

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Usage percentage over the past cycles · How much of your plan allowance you've used across recent billing periods

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Finished v/s Failed over the year · Long-term success rate trend across the past 12 months

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Total runs distribution · Run volume breakdown for the last 6 months

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Charts display "Not enough data to show this graph" until your integration has processed sufficient run history. They will populate automatically — no action needed on your part.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: *** Quick Health Check Use this as your daily 30-second routine:

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Look at Today → Failed. If it's above zero, go to Workflow Runs, filter by Failed, and investigate.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: If Runs Remaining is approaching zero, contact Cloudify to increase your plan volume before it runs out.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: If this is non-zero, you're over your plan limit. Review with your Cloudify account manager.

chunks.title: Adding a Company
chunks.text: This section on adding a company via the Company VAT app is crucial for enhancing your Pipedrive CRM with accurate, up-to-date VAT information:

chunks.title: Adding a Company
chunks.text: Streamlined Data Entry: Quickly populate your Pipedrive records with official VAT data, saving time and reducing manual input errors.

chunks.title: Adding a Company
chunks.text: Data Accuracy: By pulling information directly from VAT databases, you ensure that your company records are precise and compliant with current regulations.

chunks.title: Adding a Company
chunks.text: Efficiency: The integration of VAT lookup within the Pipedrive interface means you can update records without switching between multiple systems.

chunks.title: Adding a Company
chunks.text: Real-time Verification: Verify and update company details on the spot, particularly useful when dealing with new clients or updating existing records.

chunks.title: Adding a Company
chunks.text: Compliance Support: Easily accessing and updating VAT information helps maintain compliance with tax regulations and improves the accuracy of your financial reporting.

chunks.title: Adding a Company
chunks.text: *** How Does It Work? Open a company inside your Pipedrive CRM.

chunks.title: Adding a Company
chunks.text: Adding a Company On the right side of the window, you will see a CRM card named "Company VAT Lookup". Click "Search Company".

chunks.title: Adding a Company
chunks.text: Adding a Company A search window will pop up. Select a country and enter the VAT number or company name in the search dialogue box (use the CVR number if Denmark is selected).

chunks.title: Adding a Company
chunks.text: Click "Add" for the company you want to add. This will populate all the organisation's data into the company currently open in your Pipedrive CRM, based on the mappings you defined.

chunks.title: Adding a Company
chunks.text: Adding a Company After the successful addition, close the window and refresh the page to see the newly inserted data.

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: The mapping feature is vital for your business's VAT management in Pipedrive. Here's why it's important:

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: Compliance: Accurate mapping ensures your VAT data aligns with country-specific regulations, helping you stay compliant.

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: Data Integrity: Proper field mapping maintains consistency between your VAT information and Pipedrive records, reducing errors in reporting and calculations.

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: Efficiency: Customised mappings streamline your VAT-related workflows, saving time and reducing manual data entry.

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: Flexibility: The ability to create new properties allows you to adapt the system to your unique business needs and local VAT requirements.

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: Accuracy in Reporting: Correct mappings lead to more accurate VAT reports, which is crucial for financial management and audits.

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: Scalability: As your business expands to new countries, you can easily set up country-specific mappings, supporting your growth.

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: *** How Does It Work? Country Selection — Select the country from the drop-down box.

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: You can select only one country at a time to set mappings.

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: Map basic company data for your selected country. The following fields are available for Denmark, UK, Sweden, Australia, Norway, Switzerland, and Finland: company number, company name, country name, company address, industry code, legal form, company registration date, and status.

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: Denmark — registration number, phone, and email

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: Norway — municipality, industry description, state, zip code, and extra information

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: Switzerland — state, zip code, capital nominal

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window
chunks.text: UK — capital nominal Data sources: Australia: Australian Business Registry Services (ABRS)

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window

chunks.title: Setting Up the Mapping Window

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Set up Customer Search Rules to seamlessly synchronize customer information between Pipedrive and Fortnox, ensuring data consistency and avoiding duplicate entries. The integration actively searches for customers based on your defined parameters — if a match is found, that record is used; otherwise, a new customer profile is created to maintain a comprehensive database.

chunks.text: Customer Matching Rules Why Customer Matching Rules Matter

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Customer matching rules are crucial because they:

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Prevent duplicate customers: By accurately matching Pipedrive companies and contacts to existing Business Central customers, you avoid creating duplicate records in Business Central.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Ensure data consistency: Matching rules help maintain consistent customer data between Pipedrive and Business Central, ensuring that both systems have the most up-to-date information.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Streamline customer creation: When a match is not found, the app automatically creates a new customer in Business Central, saving you time and effort.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Simplify customer management: Properly configured matching rules make it easier to manage your customer relationships across both platforms.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Define Search Parameters: Set search preferences to match Pipedrive companies with Microsoft Business Central customers using specific fields, reducing duplicates by verifying existing records. Select a field (such as Organization Name) from a drop-down in Pipedrive for the customer sync rules and select a corresponding field (Customer Name) from the drop-down in Microsoft Business Central. Click "Save".

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Enable Primary Contact Sync: This feature is essential for businesses dealing directly with consumers. It allows the seamless addition of individual contacts from Pipedrive to Microsoft Business Central as customers when there's no associated company. Therefore, if this is the case, check “Enable Primary Contact Sync.” From the "Pipedrive Contact Identifier" dropdown menu, select the Pipedrive field that uniquely identifies your contacts, such as person name and email.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: From the "Microsoft Business Central Contact Field" dropdown menu, select the corresponding field in Microsoft Business Central that should be used to match and identify the same contact. This should also be a unique identifier like an email address or customer number in Microsoft Business Central. Click "Next".

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Select one of two options for handling the customer number when a customer is created in Microsoft Business Central: You can select whether Microsoft Business Central creates the customer number or take it from Pipedrive when creating new customer records.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Microsoft Business Central Customer Number Field: This option is conditional based on the previous selection.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Select the Pipedrive field that will store the value of the auto-generated Microsoft Business Central customer number. You can also choose not to store it anywhere in Pipedrive. It helps with integrated tracking, or you can opt not to retain this number within Pipedrive for a cleaner dataset.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Or you can choose to take the customer number from Pipedrive, for which you need to select the Pipedrive customer number field.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: After you have selected the parameters, scroll down and click Save.

chunks.title: Customer Settings

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Streamline customer creation: By setting defaults, you reduce manual data entry and potential errors.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Maintain consistency: All new customers will have the same baseline settings unless overridden by Pipedrive data.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: The company default mapping is applied to fill key fields with preset values during new customer creation in Microsoft Business Central from Pipedrive when certain data is missing.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Set default values for key fields to facilitate customer and invoice creation in Microsoft Business Central. These default values will be applied automatically whenever a new customer is created. Select the options that fit your preference and click "Save".

chunks.title: Connect Business Central

chunks.title: Connect Business Central
chunks.text: Click "Start". Click “Connect Microsoft Business Central” to connect your Microsoft Business Central account.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central
chunks.text: You will be asked to input your Microsoft Business Central credentials. First, fill in the email ID connected to your Microsoft Business Central account. Click "Next".

chunks.title: Connect Business Central
chunks.text: You will receive a successful message. Click anywhere on the screen to move to the next step.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central

chunks.title: Connect Business Central

chunks.title: Customer Search Rule
chunks.text: Set up Customer Search Rules to seamlessly synchronize customer information between Pipedrive and Microsoft Business Central, ensuring data consistency and avoiding duplicate entries. The integration actively searches for customers based on your defined parameters; if a match is found, that record is used; otherwise, a new customer profile is created to maintain a comprehensive database.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rule
chunks.text: You can configure company matching criteria by selecting a field in Pipedrive (e.g., Organization Name, Email) corresponding to the chosen Microsoft Business Central field. This ensures both platforms refer to the same company data when syncing information, maintaining consistency across systems.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rule
chunks.text: This feature is essential for businesses dealing directly with consumers, allowing the seamless addition of individual contacts from Pipedrive to Microsoft Business Central as customers when there's no associated company. Therefore, if this is the case, check “Enable Primary Contact Sync.” From the "Pipedrive Contact Identifier" dropdown menu, select the Pipedrive field that uniquely identifies your contacts, such as person name and email.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rule
chunks.text: From the "Microsoft Business Central Contact Field" dropdown menu, select the corresponding field in Microsoft Business Central that should be used to match and identify the same contact. This should also be a unique identifier like an email address or customer number in Microsoft Business Central. Click "Next".

chunks.title: Invoice Order
chunks.text: Customize how invoices or orders are generated in Microsoft Business Central by linking them to your Pipedrive sales flow.

chunks.title: Invoice Order
chunks.text: Select a Pipeline from the drop-down menu:

chunks.title: Invoice Order
chunks.text: This step allows you to link the creation of invoices or orders to a specific sales pipeline in Pipedrive. It ensures that the invoices or orders are generated at the right time in the sales process, improving efficiency and reducing the risk of errors associated with manual entry.

chunks.title: Invoice Order
chunks.text: Select the Deal Stage from the drop-down menu:

chunks.title: Invoice Order
chunks.text: Here, you select the particular stage within the sales pipeline that will trigger the creation of an invoice or order in Microsoft Business Central. This ensures the invoicing process aligns perfectly with your established sales flow.

chunks.title: Invoice Order
chunks.text: Choose the Order/Invoice from the drop-down menu:

chunks.title: Invoice Order
chunks.text: This action involves creating a draft invoice/order as per the requirement.

chunks.title: Invoice Order
chunks.text: After selecting the required options, click "Add Pipeline".

chunks.title: Invoice Order
chunks.text: The pipeline will be added. Click "Next".

chunks.title: Invoice Order
chunks.text: Note: You can add more pipelines as per your requirements by clicking on Add Pipeline. Feel free to click Get Guided Installation if you require assistance from Cloudify experts regarding the installation steps.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Product Sync Rules define how products from Pipedrive are matched with those in Microsoft Business Central, enabling a simple field-based matching or a direct connection without searching to ensure accurate product syncing and invoicing.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Simple search This feature is used to match products between Pipedrive and Microsoft Business Central by correlating a specific field, such as SKU or product number. It's particularly useful for users who have long product lists. Choose the corresponding field in Pipedrive and Microsoft Business Central for automatic identification from the respective dropdowns.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Direct Link You can connect products directly without searching. This option is useful for users who have short product lists. Map the Pipedrive fields with the Microsoft Business Central fields and click "Save Mappings".

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Advance Settings This option is useful when a product is not found in the search. It offers three options, which are:

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Skip invoice generation Select this option if you prefer not to create an invoice when a product isn't found in Microsoft Business Central.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Use a default item When an item is not found in Microsoft Business Central, it will use a default item from Microsoft Business Central to generate the invoice. If you select this option, you must specify a default item from your Microsoft Business Central item list.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Create a new item in Microsoft Business Central

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: This option automatically generates a new item entry in Microsoft Business Central when a matching product isn't found using product details from Pipedrive.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Sync deals which do not have products associated with them

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: This option is applicable when there are no products in a deal and the user wants to sync the deal. You can check this option. Select the product and click "Finish".

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Select a default item to add an overall discount as a line item

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Opt for this feature to incorporate invoice-level discounts as line items in Microsoft Business Central when chosen. This enables you to apply a standard discount to entire deals, effortlessly showcasing it as a default product within the Pipedrive deal.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: These settings help you manage how customer information is transferred and maintained, preventing duplicates and ensuring the right data is available in both systems.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: *** Customer Matching Rules Why Customer Matching Rules Matter

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: By accurately matching Pipedrive companies and contacts to existing Xero customers, you avoid creating duplicate records in Xero.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Matching rules help maintain consistent customer data between Pipedrive and Xero, keeping information up to date across both systems.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: When a match is not found, the app automatically creates a new customer in Xero, saving you time and effort.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Properly configured matching rules make it easier to manage customer relationships across both platforms.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: In the Pipedrive dropdown under Organisation Matching Criteria, select the company property you want to use to identify the customer (e.g., CVR).

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: In the Xero dropdown, select the corresponding customer field (e.g., Corporate Identification Num.).

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Check the box labelled Enable Primary Contact Sync.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: In the Pipedrive dropdown under Contact Matching Criteria, select the contact property you want to use to identify the customer (e.g., Phone Number).

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: In the Xero dropdown, select the corresponding customer field (e.g., Phone Number).

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Option 1 — Let Xero generate the customer number

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Choose whether to store the generated number in a Pipedrive property.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Select Use customer number from Pipedrive.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Select the Pipedrive property that contains the number you want to use as the Xero customer number.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Carefully review your settings to ensure they align with your business requirements. If everything looks correct, click Save to apply your changes.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Why Customer Default Mappings Are Important

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Ensure all required Xero fields are filled — these mappings provide values for fields that Xero requires when creating a new customer.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Streamline customer creation — by setting defaults, you reduce manual data entry and potential errors.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Maintain consistency — all new customers will have the same baseline settings unless overridden by Pipedrive data.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Go to the Customer Default Mappings section in your integration settings.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: You'll see a list of required Xero fields: Payment Terms, Customer Group, VAT Zone, Currency, and Invoice Layout.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: For each field, click the dropdown menu next to the field name and select the appropriate default value from the list.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: After setting your preferred defaults for all required fields, save your changes.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: *** Field Mappings (Company and Contact)

chunks.text: Ensure data consistency — match the right information between Pipedrive and Xero.

chunks.title: Customer Settings

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Save time — automate the transfer of customer data, reducing manual entry.

chunks.title: Customer Settings

chunks.title: Customer Settings

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: CVR Number (or equivalent business identifier)

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Email Phone Number Address After setting your preferred mappings, save your changes.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Go to the Contact field mappings section in your integration settings.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Follow the same process as for Company field mappings, paying special attention to these key fields:

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Customer Name — map this to the Pipedrive Full name field.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: Email Phone Number Address Using Full name is preferable to mapping separate First name and Last name fields, as it ensures the complete name is transferred correctly.

chunks.title: Customer Settings
chunks.text: After setting your preferred mappings, save your changes.

chunks.text: Choose a Pipedrive field (e.g., SKU) and match it with a Xero field (e.g., Product Number).

chunks.text: When creating an invoice or quote, the integration will use this identifier to find the correct product in Xero.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Welcome to the Pipedrive-Xero Integration Setup Guide. This comprehensive resource will help you connect your Pipedrive and Xero accounts, enabling seamless data synchronization and workflow automation between these powerful platforms.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Integration Benefits By integrating Pipedrive with Xero, your organization can:

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Automate invoice/quote generation based on Pipedrive deal stages

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Ensure real-time synchronization of customer data across both platforms

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Access up-to-date financial insights directly within Pipedrive

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Significantly reduce time spent on manual data entry and reconciliation

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Enhance financial reporting with integrated sales and accounting data

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The table below shows what data is synced between Pipedrive and Xero. The data flow is largely unidirectional from Pipedrive to Xero except for the invoice/quote PDF copy imported back into Pipedrive as well as updated booked-invoice data synced into Pipedrive.

chunks.title: One Click Invoice Quote
chunks.text: -Pipedrive Xero integration by Cloudify facilitates one-click creation of invoices/quotes directly from Pipedrive deals irrespective of the deal stage.

chunks.title: One Click Invoice Quote
chunks.text: Selecting "I'll do it manually" skips automation and takes you to the Cloudify dashboard, allowing you to update invoices from any Pipedrive deal stage.

chunks.title: One Click Invoice Quote
chunks.text: Once you click on the Dashboard, follow these streamlined steps to complete a manual sync:

chunks.title: One Click Invoice Quote
chunks.text: Access the invoice: Go to any invoice on the dashboard you wish to update and click Review and Sync. The manual sync window will immediately appear on your screen.

chunks.title: One Click Invoice Quote
chunks.text: Enter basic details: Select your contact, currency, tax, and account details to get started.

chunks.title: One Click Invoice Quote
chunks.text: Set invoice terms: Choose specific details such as the Invoice date, Due date, Status, and Tax preferences.

chunks.title: One Click Invoice Quote
chunks.text: Add products: Click + Add Line Item to include products to your draft. To adjust specific item settings, click Customize Accounts, Taxes and Amounts.

chunks.title: One Click Invoice Quote
chunks.text: Product Availability: You can only use the "+ Add Line Item" button for products that are already present in Xero.

chunks.title: One Click Invoice Quote
chunks.text: Adjust the invoice (Optional): Click the three-dots menu to Split your invoice by percentage or Duplicate it.

chunks.title: One Click Invoice Quote
chunks.text: The option to split an invoice is only available while it remains in the 'DRAFT' stage.

chunks.title: One Click Invoice Quote
chunks.text: Finish and sync: Click Save Progress if you need to finish later, or Sync to Xero to push the draft Xero. You can view the final invoice in the deal's attachments or notes.

chunks.text: Define how products from Pipedrive are matched with items in Xero, enabling field-based matching or direct connection for accurate product syncing and invoicing.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Product Sync Rules define how products from Pipedrive are matched with products in Xero, enabling simple field-based matching or a direct connection without searching ensuring accurate product syncing and invoicing.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: *** Simple Search Use this feature to match products between Pipedrive and Xero by correlating a specific field, such as Product Code in Pipedrive and Item Code in Xero. This is particularly useful for users who have long product lists.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Choose the corresponding fields in Pipedrive and Xero for automatic identification from the respective dropdowns.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: *** Direct Link Select this method to link specific products one-to-one between Pipedrive and Xero directly. This option is particularly beneficial when the product count is low, allowing for precise, manual matching of each product.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: *** Advanced Settings These settings apply when a product is not found during the search. Choose one of the three fallback options below:

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Select this option if you prefer not to create an invoice when a product isn't found in Xero.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: When an item is not found in Xero, a default item from Xero will be used to generate the invoice. If you select this option, you must specify a default product from your Xero item list.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: This option automatically generates a new product entry in Xero when a matching item isn't found, using product details from Pipedrive.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: *** Sync Deals Without Associated Products

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: This option lets you create an invoice using just the deal value — useful if you don't use products in your Pipedrive deals. Check the checkbox and select a placeholder product to handle this scenario.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Select an item from Xero to reflect discounts from Pipedrive deals. This selected item will appear as an overall discount line in the invoice or quote.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Once done, click Save. Your installation is now complete.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Configure automated API polling — pull data from external systems on a schedule without waiting for a webhook push.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: The Polling page lets you set up scheduled API polling inside Lighthouse Flows. Instead of waiting for an external system to push data, a polling configuration calls an external API at regular intervals and pulls data automatically.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Use polling when your source system does not support outbound webhooks. If it can push data to Lighthouse in real time, use a webhook trigger instead — it's more efficient.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: *** Summary Counters Three counters at the top show the current state of your polling configurations at a glance.

chunks.text: Click + New Polling Config in the top-right corner. The creation form has four sections — work through them top to bottom.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: *** Schedule Configuration Set how often Lighthouse should call the external API.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Two modes are available: Choose from preset intervals — Every 5 min, Every 15 min, Every 30 min, Every hour, Every 6 hours, or Daily. The current schedule expression is shown at the bottom of the panel.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Enter a custom expression directly — supports rate() and cron() syntax for precise scheduling.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: cron(0 12 ? *) · Run daily at 12:00 PM UTC

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: 0 /6 · Run every 6 hours *** HTTP Request Configuration

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Define the API endpoint Lighthouse should call on each poll.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Two modes are available: Fill in the endpoint URL, HTTP method, headers, query parameters, authentication, and request body using form fields.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Write a JavaScript handler function directly — full control over how the request is made and how the response is processed.

chunks.title: Polling

chunks.title: Polling

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Query Parameters · Optional · URL query parameters appended to the endpoint

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Authentication · Optional · Configure how to authenticate — defaults to No Authentication

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Request Body · Optional · JSON payload for POST, PUT, or PATCH requests

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: *** Response Parser, Retry Logic, Pagination & Filter

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Response Parser · Always · Extract specific data from the API response using a JSON Path — e.g. data.items. Add Custom Logic (JavaScript) to transform the response before it's passed downstream

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Retry Logic · Optional · Automatically retry failed poll attempts. Toggle on to configure retry behaviour

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Pagination · Optional · Handle multi-page API responses — toggle on when the API returns paginated results

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Incremental Polling Filter · Optional · Only process records that are new or updated since the last poll — prevents reprocessing the same data

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Click Create Configuration to save, or Cancel to discard.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Contact Cloudify before creating a polling configuration. Getting the endpoint URL, authentication, schedule, and response parser correct requires knowledge of your source API. Cloudify will typically configure these as part of your integration delivery.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Use polling when your source system cannot push data to Lighthouse when something changes. If it supports webhooks, use a webhook trigger instead — it's real-time and more efficient.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: Quick Setup gives you six preset intervals in one click. Advanced lets you write a custom rate() or cron() expression for precise timing — for example, running only on weekdays at a specific time.

chunks.title: Polling
chunks.text: It ensures only new or updated records are processed on each poll — so if your API returns 1,000 records but only 5 are new, only those 5 are passed downstream. This prevents duplicate processing.

chunks.title: Schedule
chunks.text: Manage cron and rate schedules that trigger your Flows automatically — no webhook or external push required.

chunks.title: Schedule
chunks.text: The Schedule page lets you define time-based triggers for Lighthouse Flows. A schedule fires a Flow automatically at a set interval or specific time — using AWS EventBridge rate() or cron() expressions.

chunks.title: Schedule
chunks.text: Schedule vs Polling Schedule — fires a Flow trigger at a set time. No external data is fetched.

chunks.title: Schedule
chunks.text: Polling — calls an external API at a set interval to pull data.

chunks.title: Schedule
chunks.text: Use Schedule when you want a Flow to run at a specific time. Use Polling when you need Lighthouse to retrieve data from an external API on a cadence.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Control how your Shopify customers are matched and created in Exact Online. This page covers three areas: how customers are matched, what defaults are applied when creating new ones, and how individual fields are mapped.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Sync Rules How do you want to match your customers?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: When a Shopify order comes in, the integration needs to find the right customer in Exact Online. This setting tells it which field to use for that lookup.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose a field that is always filled out and unique to each customer. Email address works best for most businesses — it's reliably present and avoids false matches between customers with similar names.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Make sure the selected Shopify field is never empty on your orders. If the field is blank, the integration cannot find or create a customer and will trigger an error.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: If you use Shopify POS and some orders have no customer attached, enable "Use a Default Customer for Point of Sale (POS) Orders".

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: When active, the integration will automatically assign a customer named POS Customer – Cloudify in Exact Online to any POS order where no customer is present. This keeps your invoices clean without requiring manual intervention.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Default Mappings What are your default settings for new customers?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: When a Shopify customer cannot be matched to an existing account in Exact Online, the integration creates a new one. These default settings define the financial values applied to that new account automatically.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Configure these to match how your business handles sales — so every new customer is created with the right settings from day one, without manual edits in Exact Online.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Field · Description VAT code · The default VAT code applied to sales transactions for new customers.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: GL account · The default general ledger account used for revenue.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Journal · The default journal (book) where sales invoices are recorded.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Payment condition · The default payment terms applied to invoices (e.g. 21 days).

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Sales currency · The default currency for new customer accounts.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Shipping method · The default shipping method applied when creating new customers.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Source · The account classification (source) assigned to new customers.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: These defaults only apply when a new customer is created in Exact Online. Existing matched accounts are not affected.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Customer Field Mappings How should customer data fields be mapped between Shopify and Exact Online?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Field mappings control exactly which Shopify data gets written into which Exact Online account field when a customer is created or updated.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Some common fields are pre-mapped for you out of the box:

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Exact Online Field · Shopify Field · Status

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Account name (Required) · Customer Name · Mapped

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: You can add, edit, or remove mappings as needed using the Create new Shopify field button. Mappings are split into two tabs:

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: General — Core account fields such as name, email, and phone.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Invoice address — Billing address fields synced to the Exact Online account.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Click Save after making any changes to your field mappings. Unsaved changes will not take effect on your next sync.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: This page controls when invoices are created in Exact Online, what type they are, what extra details get included, and how invoice data fields are mapped from your Shopify orders.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Sync Rules Automatically create Exact Online invoices

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: When this toggle is on, the integration creates invoices in Exact Online automatically — no manual action needed on your end.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Turn it off if you prefer to create invoices manually from the dashboard. This gives you full control over which orders get invoiced and when.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose the Shopify order status that triggers invoice creation:

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: When Fulfilled · After the order has been shipped

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: When Paid · As soon as payment is recorded in Shopify

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: When Created (default) · The moment the order is placed in Shopify

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Pick the trigger that matches your business flow. If you invoice before shipping, use When Created. If you only invoice after goods are dispatched, use When Fulfilled.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose how the invoice is created in Exact Online:

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Type · What it means Open Invoice · The invoice is created as a draft — it's open and can still be edited in Exact Online before being finalized.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Incorporated Invoice · The invoice is created as processed (incorporated) — it's immediately finalized and posted to your accounts.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Use Open Invoice if your team reviews invoices before posting them. Use Incorporated Invoice if you want everything finalized automatically without any manual step in Exact Online.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Additional Options Fine-tune how the integration handles shipping charges, refunds, and other invoice details.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Include shipping charges When enabled, any shipping cost on the Shopify order is added as a separate line on the Exact Online invoice — so your invoice reflects the full amount the customer was charged.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: You'll also select which item code and GL account to use for shipping lines, so they're posted correctly in your books.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Exact Online credit notes from Shopify refunds

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: When a customer gets a refund in Shopify, this option automatically creates a matching credit note in Exact Online — keeping your accounting in sync without any manual work.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: You can configure exactly how refunds should be handled using the dropdown that appears when this option is enabled.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Configure both shipping and refund settings before going live. Leaving these on Select means the integration won't know where to post those amounts when they come through.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Field Mappings control which Shopify order data gets written into the invoice header in Exact Online.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Out of the box, the following is pre-mapped:

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Exact Online field · Pulled from Shopify

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Description · Order Note If a Shopify field is empty on an order, the corresponding Exact Online field will either be left blank or fall back to the system default.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: You can add more mappings using the Create new Shopify field button — for example, mapping a Shopify order tag or custom field to an Exact Online invoice field.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Click Save after making any changes. Nothing takes effect until you save.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Before integrating Shopify with Exact Online, make sure you meet the requirements below for a smooth setup.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Complete all prerequisites before starting installation. Missing any of these can block the connection partway through setup.

chunks.title: Prerequisites

chunks.title: Prerequisites

chunks.title: Prerequisites
