chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Know how your order management, payment collection, and fulfillment work today. The integration's sync rules (when to invoice, how to match customers and products, how to handle tax) map directly onto these processes — so a clear picture up front makes configuration faster and more accurate.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: This page controls how the integration handles your products — how it finds them in Exact Online, what happens when a product isn't found, and how tax and accounts are applied on invoices.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Sync Rules Choose a product search method

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: When a Shopify order syncs, the integration needs to find the right product in Exact Online to put on the invoice. Choose the method that fits how your catalog is set up.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Simple Search The integration automatically looks up the product in Exact Online by comparing a field from Shopify against a field in Exact Online.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: For example: match Shopify Title against Exact Online Description — if they match, the integration uses that product on the invoice.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: This works well for larger catalogs where you want matching to happen without any manual work.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Make sure the fields you select are consistently filled in and formatted the same way on both sides. A mismatch in spelling or casing can cause a product not to be found.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Direct Link Manually connect each Shopify product to a specific product in Exact Online yourself. Once linked, the integration always uses that exact product — no searching involved.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: This is the best option for smaller catalogs where you want full control over which Exact Online product ends up on each invoice.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Getting your product match right matters. If a product isn't found, Exact Online can't generate an accurate invoice — and the fallback option below will be used instead.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** If a product is not found in Exact Online

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Sometimes a Shopify product won't have a match in Exact Online. Choose what you want the integration to do in that situation.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Skip invoice generation The integration stops and does not create an invoice for that order. Use this if you'd rather investigate manually than have an invoice created with the wrong product.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Use a default product The integration still creates the invoice, but uses a pre-selected Exact Online product as a stand-in. Only the product code of that default product is used — all other details like price, quantity, and description are taken directly from the Shopify order.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: This keeps your invoicing running without interruption, even when a product match isn't found.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: The integration automatically creates a brand new product in Exact Online using the details from the Shopify order. You'll also select a default GL account to assign to any newly created products.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose this if you want your Exact Online product list to stay in sync with whatever you sell on Shopify.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Tax settings Exclude Shopify Tax from Exact Online invoices

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Shopify calculates and displays tax on orders. Exact Online also applies VAT to invoices based on its own VAT codes.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: If both systems apply tax, you could end up with double taxation on your invoices. Enable this checkbox to strip out the Shopify tax entirely — so only Exact Online's VAT rules are applied when the invoice is created.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: This is relevant if your Exact Online VAT codes are already set up correctly. Once enabled, tax on Shopify orders is ignored and Exact Online handles all VAT calculation on its own.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Default sales account This is the general ledger (GL) account where revenue gets posted when no specific account is set on the product itself. It also acts as the fallback account for shipping charges.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Set this to the revenue account in Exact Online that best represents your general sales income.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Item creation settings If the integration creates new products in Exact Online, this setting controls the default unit applied to those items (for example: pcs, hour, minute).

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose the unit that matches how you typically sell — so new products are created correctly without needing manual edits in Exact Online afterwards.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Click Save after making any changes. Nothing takes effect until you save.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Automate Shopify payout reconciliation in Xero — journal entries for payments, fees, and payouts.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: The Bookkeeping section lets you automate how Shopify payouts are recorded in Xero. When enabled, the integration creates journal entries for Shopify Payments, fees, and bank payouts — so your books stay accurate without manual work.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: *** How Bookkeeping Works Understanding how your Shopify transactions move to Xero helps you keep track of your cash flow and reconciliation.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: The 3-Step Process As soon as a customer pays, the app creates a draft entry in Xero to record the sale and the expected funds.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Payments are held by your processor (Stripe/PayPal) in a "Clearing Account" until they are ready to be paid out to your bank.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: When the payout hits your bank, the system automatically moves the funds from the clearing account to your bank account and records any fees.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Here's what a typical payout looks like when it's recorded in Xero:

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Clearing · −\$250.00 · The payment leaves the clearing account

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Fee · −\$7.50 · Shopify's processing fee is deducted

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Bank · +\$242.50 · The net amount lands in your bank account

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: The net amount (\$242.50) is balanced against your bank statement automatically.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: *** Enable Bookkeeping Toggle Automated Bookkeeping Sync to enable or disable this feature. When disabled, no payout-related journal entries are created in Xero.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: *** Payout Mode Choose how payouts are recorded in Xero:

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Cloudify will automatically push your payout data into the Xero journal. No manual action needed — payouts sync as they happen.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Your payouts from Shopify will be available in the Cloudify Dashboard. You can review them and push to Xero manually when you're ready.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Not applicable for Draft Invoices. Journal entries are only created when your invoice type is set to something other than Draft.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: This section lets you set up preferences for adding journal entries to Xero. Journal entries can be created for Shopify Payments (to record customer payments), Shopify fees, and payouts to your bank account. This ensures accurate bookkeeping, with each entry going into the correct journal and account.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Shopify processes merchant payouts cumulatively by consolidating multiple payouts and disbursing the total amount in a scheduled transaction. Set your preferences for journal entries using the settings below.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: You can click "Send to accountant" to share these settings with your accountant for review.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Bookkeeping Settings Configure which Xero accounts each type of transaction is posted to:

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Payout Account (Bank A/c) · Select your bank account · Where Shopify deposits your money — most often your Bank account.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Shopify Payments Clearing account · CF-00000 — Shopify-Payments Clearing · The offset account for Shopify Payments (e.g. Shopify Payments clearing). Add it from the Invoice sync rules settings.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Shopify Fee account · CF-30000 — Shopify Fees · Account for Shopify transaction fees.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Select Adjustment · Select · Technical regulations account.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Select Reserved · Select · Account for amount Shopify is holding back.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Click Save when you're done configuring your bookkeeping accounts.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: The Shopify Payments Clearing account and Shopify Fee account are Cloudify-generated accounts in Xero. The Payout Account, Adjustment, and Reserved accounts need to be selected from your existing Xero chart of accounts.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Configure how Shopify customers are matched, created, and mapped to Xero contacts.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: The Customer tab controls how Shopify customer data flows into Xero. There are three sections to configure: Sync Rules, Default Mappings, and Customer Field Mappings.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: *** Sync Rules How do you want to match your customers?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: When a Shopify order comes in, the integration needs to find the right Xero contact. You configure this by choosing which Shopify field to match against which Xero field.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Select the most reliable field for identifying your customers. Choose something that's always filled out and unique to each customer — email addresses work well for most businesses.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Ensure selected Shopify fields are not empty to avoid triggering errors. If a customer's field is blank in Shopify, the match will fail.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: POS Default Customer Use a Default Customer for Point of Sale (POS) Order

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: If a Shopify POS order has no customer associated, the integration creates a customer named "POS Customer – Cloudify" in Xero. This customer is then assigned to all invoices created for POS orders where no customer is present.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Enable this if you process POS sales where customers don't provide their details.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: *** Default Mappings What are your default settings for new customers?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: When the integration creates a new customer in Xero from Shopify data, it uses these defaults to fill in key fields:

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Select currency · Currency for financial transactions · United States Dollar

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Select branding theme · Theme for invoice and quote presentation in Xero · Standard

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Select invoice due date · Number of days after the invoice date before it's considered due · Days after the invoice date

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Select sales account · Accounting ledger account used for recording sales transactions · 4000 – Sale of Goods

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Sales default amounts are · Whether sales amounts are tax-inclusive, tax-exclusive, or no tax · Tax inclusive

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: If you sell to multiple countries and want to post revenue to different Xero sales accounts based on the customer's country, enable this option.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Once enabled, select the countries you want to configure and assign a specific sales account for each one.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: This is useful if you need to separate domestic vs. international revenue in your Xero reporting.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: *** Customer Field Mappings How should customer data fields be mapped?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: This section controls exactly which Shopify customer fields map to which Xero contact fields. It determines how customer information is transferred when creating a new contact or updating an existing one in Xero.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Some common fields are pre-mapped for your convenience. To update a mapped field, click on the box and select your preferred Shopify field. You can remove an existing mapping by clicking the "Clear" button.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Field mappings are organized into three tabs:

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: General Core contact details like name, email, and phone.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Contact name (Required) · Customer Name · Mapped

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Billing Address Maps the customer's Shopify billing address fields to the corresponding Xero contact address fields.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Delivery Address Maps the customer's Shopify shipping/delivery address fields to the corresponding Xero contact address fields.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: You can also create custom Shopify fields using the "Create new Shopify field" button if your store captures data that doesn't map to a standard field (e.g. a company registration number or VAT ID).

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Click Save when you're done configuring your field mappings.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Each Shopify order becomes its own Xero invoice — detailed, easy to reconcile.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: How It Works Every Shopify order is pushed to Xero as a separate invoice with full line-item details — products, quantities, prices, tax, shipping, and discounts all included.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Automated Triggers You choose when an order gets pushed to Xero based on its Shopify status:

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Order Created — pushes the invoice as soon as the order is placed.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Order Fulfilled — waits until you mark the order as fulfilled.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Order Paid — waits until payment is confirmed.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: You also choose what type of invoice is generated in Xero.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Customer & Product Sync The integration searches Xero for existing customers and products that match the Shopify order. If no match is found, it creates them in Xero for you.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Data flows from Shopify to Xero — not the other way around.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Shipping & Refunds Shipping charges are included on the Xero invoice. When a refund is issued in Shopify on a previously synced order, a credit note is generated in Xero automatically.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Make sure shipping and refund options are enabled in your configuration.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: *** Configuration Tabs Once you select Individual Order Mode, you'll see three tabs to set up:

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Set up sync rules that control how Shopify customers are matched to Xero contacts. Define matching fields, handle missing contacts, and configure POS default customers.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Map Shopify products to Xero items and assign the correct revenue accounts.

chunks.title: Individual Order Mode
chunks.text: Choose invoice type, due dates, reference format, and how shipping and refunds appear on invoices.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Control when Xero invoices are created, what type they are, and how shipping and refunds are handled.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: The Invoice tab controls when and how Xero invoices are generated from your Shopify orders. There are two sections: Sync Rules and Additional Options.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: *** Sync Rules Automatically Create (Xero) Invoices

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: This toggle controls whether invoices are created in Xero automatically when a Shopify order reaches a certain status.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: When enabled, choose the trigger that fits your workflow:

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: When Fulfilled (after shipping) · Invoice is created once you mark the order as fulfilled in Shopify.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: When Paid (payment recorded in Shopify) · Invoice is created once payment is confirmed.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: When Created (order created in Shopify) · Invoice is created immediately when the order is placed.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Turn this off if you prefer to create invoices manually from the Cloudify dashboard instead of using automated triggers.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Invoice Type in Xero Choose what type of invoice is generated in Xero:

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Draft Invoice · Created as a draft — you or your accountant review and approve it before it's finalized.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Awaiting-Approval Invoice · Created and queued for approval in Xero.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Awaiting-Payment Invoice · Created as approved and ready for payment.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Paid Invoice · Created and marked as fully paid immediately. Payment is applied automatically using clearing accounts.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Pick the type that matches your accounting workflow. If you're unsure, Draft Invoice is the safest starting point — it gives you a chance to review before anything is finalized.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: When you select Paid Invoice, Cloudify automatically applies payment using dedicated clearing accounts based on the Shopify payment method (Cash, Shopify Payments, or other).

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Click "Edit Xero Accounts" to configure which Xero account each payment type is recorded to:

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Shopify Payments · CF-00000 — Shopify-Payments Clearing

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Gift Card · CF-80000 — Shopify Gift Cards

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: All Other Payment Types · CF-60001 — Non-Shopify Payments Clearing

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: These are Cloudify-generated accounts in Xero. They're created automatically — you don't need to set them up manually, but you can reassign them to different accounts if needed.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: *** Additional Options These settings let you configure shipping, refunds, and email notifications on your Xero invoices.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Include Shipping Charges Enable this to have shipping charges appear as a line item on your Xero invoice. Once enabled, select how shipping should be represented in Xero (e.g. which account or item it maps to).

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Enable this to automatically create credit notes in Xero when a refund is issued in Shopify. Once enabled, configure how refunds are handled in Xero (e.g. which account they're posted to).

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Enable this to send automated invoice emails to your customers from Xero when an invoice is created.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Configure the above settings to streamline shipping charges, credit note creation from Shopify refunds, and manage automated invoice emails to your customers.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Configure how Shopify products are matched, created, and mapped to Xero items.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: The Product tab controls how Shopify products are found and synced to Xero items. There are four sections: Sync Rules, If Product Not Found, Tax Settings, and Field Mappings.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: *** Sync Rules Choose a product search method

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: When a Shopify order comes in, the integration needs to find the matching product in Xero. You have two options:

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Automatically match products using specific fields. Select a Shopify field and a corresponding Xero field to match against.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Similar fields work best — for example, matching SKU to Product Number. If you don't use SKUs in Shopify, try matching using Product Name fields instead.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Manually link each Shopify product to a specific Xero item. Best for smaller product catalogs where you want precise control over every mapping.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: If using Simple Search, configure your matching fields:

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Title · Name Why it matters: This step is crucial for accurate invoicing and inventory management. If the product is not found, one of the fallback options below is applied — where "Skip invoice generation" is selected by default.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: When the integration can't find a matching Xero item, choose what should happen:

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Option · What It Does Skip invoice generation · The invoice is not created in Xero. This is the default.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Use a default product · Falls back to a specific Xero item you designate as the default.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Create a new product in Xero · Automatically creates the product as a new item in Xero and assigns it to your chosen Sales Account (e.g. CF-20000 — Shopify Sales).

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: If you choose "Create a new product in Xero", be aware this may create duplicate or unnecessary products if not managed carefully. Review your Xero items periodically.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: *** Tax Settings Exclude Shopify Tax from Xero invoices

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Enable this to remove taxes applied on Shopify orders when creating the Xero invoice. Only the relevant Xero tax rates will be applied instead.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Cloudify does not perform any tax calculations — it depends on your existing tax settings in Xero. Use this when your Xero tax setup should take precedence over Shopify's tax values.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: *** Field Mappings How should product data fields be mapped?

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: This section defines how product information transfers from Shopify to Xero when creating new items.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Note: This section is only applicable if you've chosen "Create a new product in Xero" as your fallback option above. The integration fetches details from the Shopify fields and syncs them to the corresponding Xero field.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Common fields are pre-mapped by default:

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: To update a mapping, click the field box and select a different Shopify field. Use "Clear" to remove a mapping, or "Create new Shopify field" if your store uses custom data that doesn't map to a standard field.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Setup
chunks.text: Choose how your Shopify sales are recorded in Xero — one invoice per order or daily summaries.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Setup
chunks.text: The first thing you'll configure is how Shopify transactions appear in Xero. You have two options:

chunks.title: Sales Posting Setup
chunks.text: Recommended for most stores. Every Shopify order creates its own Xero invoice with full line-item details. Easy to match each sale back to a specific order.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Setup
chunks.text: Best for detailed, order-level reconciliation.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Setup
chunks.text: Groups all of yesterday's sales into one invoice and refunds into one credit note in Xero. Keeps your ledger clean at high volumes.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Setup
chunks.text: Best for a simple, summarized daily view.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Setup
chunks.text: You can switch between modes at any time. Switching only affects future sales — anything already pushed to Xero stays as-is.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Setup
chunks.text: *** Switching Between Modes You can switch from one mode to the other at any time from this page.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Setup
chunks.text: Switching modes affects how your future sales data is posted to Xero. Previously pushed data will not be affected.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Setup
chunks.text: A confirmation dialog will appear when you switch. Click Confirm and Continue to apply the change.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: All of yesterday's Shopify sales grouped into one Xero invoice and one credit note — daily.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: How It Works For transactions that occurred in Shopify the previous day, Cloudify automatically aggregates them into a single Invoice (for sales) and a single Credit Note (for refunds) inside Xero.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: One invoice covering all of yesterday's sales, broken down by:

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Sales with VAT / Tax Sales without VAT / Tax Shipping with VAT / Tax Shipping without VAT / Tax

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Discounts (adjusted directly against sales)

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: One credit note covering all of yesterday's refunds, broken down by:

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Refunds with VAT / Tax Refunds with no tax (custom refunds)

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Shipping refunds Gift card refunds *** Configuration Transfer Frequency Controls when the daily summary is generated and pushed to Xero.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: The default is Daily Summary — covering transactions from 00:00:00 to 23:59:59 each day. A summarized invoice and credit note for your previous day's Shopify transactions will be generated in Xero.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: You can also use the "Send to accountant" button to manually trigger a summary push at any time.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Tax Rate Mapping Configure how Shopify tax data maps to Xero tax rates.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Setting · What It Does Default Xero Tax Rate · The tax rate shown on invoice lines. The actual tax amount still comes from Shopify.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Invoice Amounts in Xero · Choose whether amounts are Tax inclusive or Tax exclusive.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: For Shopify line items that have no tax, you assign a default Xero tax rate for each type:

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Shopify Line Type · Default Xero Tax Rate

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Shipping Fees (Tax free) · Tax Exempt (0)

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Pending Transactions (Tax free) · Tax Exempt (0)

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: How this works: If a Shopify line has tax, the integration uses the Shopify tax rate mapping above. If the line has no tax, it falls back to the default tax rate you've selected for that line type.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Xero Account Selection Choose which Xero accounts your Shopify revenue and transactions are posted to:

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Shopify Item Type · Xero Account · Purpose

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Shopify Sales Revenue · CF-20000 — Shopify Sales · Standard sales revenue from product purchases

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Shopify Shipping Revenue · CF-20001 — Shopify Shipping Revenue · Revenue from shipping and delivery fees

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Shopify Balance/Pending Transactions · CF-60002 — Shopify Balance/Pending Tran... · Clearing account for partial or pending checkout balances

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Payment Methods Map your Shopify payment methods to the correct Xero clearing accounts so payouts reconcile correctly:

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Shopify Payments · CF-00000 — Shopify-Payments Clearing

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Gift Card · CF-80000 — Shopify Gift Cards

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: All Other Payment Types · CF-60001 — Non-Shopify Payments Clearing

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: All CF- accounts are created automatically by Cloudify in your Xero org. You don't need to set them up manually. Click "View Cloudify generated accounts in Xero" to see them.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: *** Channel-Wise Sales & POS Distinction

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: To prevent mixups, orders are automatically separated based on where they came from:

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Channel · What Happens POS Channel · Point of Sale orders go to a completely separate Invoice and Credit Note.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Online & Draft · Online Store, Draft, and Manual orders go to their own invoices based on your customer mappings.

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Cloudify creates three dedicated customer records in Xero to keep these channels segregated:

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Online Sales · Shopify Online Store (Cloudify)

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Manual Orders · Shopify Manual Orders (Cloudify)

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: *** Xero References & Layout Every invoice and credit note follows a consistent naming pattern so you can find them easily:

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Invoice & Credit Note Reference — Shopify Orders Paid/Partially paid on {transaction-date} (e.g. Shopify Orders Fully/Partially Paid on 16 June 2026)

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Payment Reference in Xero — set to the actual payment method (e.g. Cash, Manual, or Credit card)

chunks.title: Sales Summary Mode
chunks.text: Partially Paid Orders — the full sale goes to the Sales Account, while the unpaid balance goes into CF-60002 (Shopify Balance/Pending Transactions). It clears to zero once the order is fully paid.

chunks.title: Common Shopify Economic Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: A customer is not present in the Shopify order. Since a customer is needed to create an invoice in Economic, it is mandatory. Please go to your Shopify order and add a customer to it. Once done click on More actions> Replay Integration.

chunks.title: Common Shopify Economic Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: SKU should not be empty SKU is not present in your product in the Shopify order. Please go to products in Shopify > Click on the product which is present in the order > Under Inventory section, Add an SKU > Save the changes.

chunks.title: Common Shopify Economic Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Invoice creation skipped You have selected the option to not create an Invoice, when a product from Shopify order is not found in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Common Shopify Economic Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Please go to Visma economic sync app in cloudify > Product Settings > Go to when a product is not found in e-conomic > Choose either to use a default product from Economic or create a new product.

chunks.title: Common Shopify Economic Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Settings are not enabled to handle shipping charges in Shopify order.

chunks.title: Common Shopify Economic Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Please go to Visma economic sync app settings in Shopify> Invoice settings > Under Additional options\_- Enable \_Include Shipping charges & select a product from the dropdown to be used as a Default Shipping charge line item.

chunks.title: Common Shopify Economic Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: (It is recommended to create a new product directly within Economic named as Shipping Charges and select it here.)

chunks.title: Common Shopify Economic Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Invalid format for e-conomic Customer number

chunks.title: Common Shopify Economic Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: A Shopify field containing letters has been mapped to be used as E-conomic Customer number. E-conomic only accepts numerical values for Customer number.

chunks.title: Common Shopify Economic Errors & Fixes
chunks.text: Please go to Visma economic sync app settings in Shopify> Customer settings > Under 'How to handle customer number in e-conomic' from the dropdown select 'Let e-conomic create customer number'

chunks.title: Subscription
chunks.text: Plans, pricing, and how to change or cancel your subscription

chunks.title: Subscription
chunks.text: The Subscription page shows your current plan, how many orders you have used this month, and the available plans. You find it in the app menu under Subscription.

chunks.title: Subscription
chunks.text: Plans are based on how many Shopify orders the app processes per month. Pick the plan that matches your monthly order volume.

chunks.title: Subscription
chunks.text: Billing period Use the Monthly / Yearly toggle at the top to switch between billing periods. Yearly billing saves 15%.

chunks.title: Subscription
chunks.text: The Scale plan is only available on monthly billing. It does not appear when the toggle is set to Yearly.

chunks.title: Subscription
chunks.text: Plans Free Trial – sync 30 real orders into e-conomic with the full feature set unlocked, then pick the plan that fits. The 30 orders are a one-time allotment, not monthly.

chunks.title: Subscription
chunks.text: Starter – every sale creates an invoice in e-conomic automatically, and you get the dashboard to see and manage all synced orders. Starter does not include refunds/credit notes, sales summary sync, bookkeeping (payout reconciliation), the payouts dashboard, or bulk sync tools.

chunks.title: Subscription
chunks.text: Growth – everything in Starter, plus: refunds automatically create credit notes, daily sales totals posted to e-conomic, Shopify Payments payouts matched to your books automatically, a dashboard showing all payout activity, and bulk-sync of past orders when getting started.

chunks.title: Subscription
chunks.text: Professional – the same complete automation as Growth, built for stores processing up to 800 orders a month.

chunks.title: Subscription
chunks.text: Scale – everything in Growth and Professional, plus a dedicated Customer Success Manager for onboarding, setup, and ongoing help. Includes 2,000 orders per month; orders above that are charged at \$0.05 each (pay as you go), so there is no hard cap.

chunks.title: Subscription
chunks.text: Comparing plans Click Compare all features below the plan cards to see a detailed table of every feature across all plans, grouped into Volume & Fees, Core Synchronization, Bookkeeping & Summary, and Account & Support.

chunks.title: Subscription

chunks.title: Subscription
