chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Welcome to the official setup guide for the Shopify to e-conomic integration. This comprehensive guide will walk you through connecting your Shopify store and e-conomic accounting system, from initial installation to advanced configuration. By the end, you'll have a fully automated financial workflow that transforms your e-commerce operations.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Integration Benefits By integrating Shopify with e-conomic, your organization can:

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Effortlessly generate invoices in e-conomic directly from Shopify orders.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Automate journal entries for Shopify payouts, fees, and refunds in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Quickly retry failed invoice syncs with a single click when errors occur.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Seamlessly synchronize product and customer data across both platforms.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The table below shows what data is synced between Shopify and Visma e-conomic. The data flow is unidirectional from Shopify to Visma e-conomic except for the invoice number synced back into Shopify order notes.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: This document outlines the essential prerequisites for successfully integrating Shopify and e-conomic. Adhering to these requirements will ensure a smooth integration process, optimal data synchronization, and secure operation.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Before starting the integration process, please ensure you have:

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: An active Shopify store with administrative access

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: An active e-conomic account with administrative rights

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Authentication credentials for both platforms

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Basic understanding of your business workflow

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: How to install and connect the Shopify e-conomic integration, step by step

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: This guide walks you through installing the app and connecting your Shopify store to your e-conomic accounting system. Setup takes just a few minutes.. When you are done, your Shopify orders will automatically become invoices in e-conomic. You do not need any technical knowledge.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Log in to your Shopify admin (the page where you manage your store).

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: In the left menu, click Apps. A search field appears at the top. Type Visma e-conomic Integration and press Enter.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: The app appears in the search results. Click on it to open the app page.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: On the app page, click the Install button.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Shopify will show you a list of permissions the app needs. This is standard for all Shopify apps. The app needs permission to read your orders, customers, and products, because this is the data it sends to e-conomic.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Click Install again to confirm. The app is now added to your store.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: After installation, the app opens with a welcome screen.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Click the green Get started button to begin the setup.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: This step links your Shopify store to your e-conomic account, so the two systems can share data.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Click the black Connect to e-conomic button. A Visma e-conomic login window opens.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: If you already have an e-conomic account: log in with your usual e-conomic username and password, and approve the connection.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: If you do not have an e-conomic account yet: you can create one in the same window before connecting.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: The login happens on Visma's own secure page. The app never sees or stores your e-conomic password.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Once you have logged in and approved, you are sent back to the app, and the connection is complete.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: If you want to see how the app works before connecting your real account, click Schedule demo instead. A team member will walk you through the setup live, free of charge.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: After connecting, you land on the You're All Set page. The app has already chosen sensible settings for you. You can use these as they are, or change them at any time.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Setting · What the app does · Why it matters

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Invoice creation: When Created · An invoice is made in e-conomic the moment an order is placed in Shopify · You never have to create invoices manually

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Customer lookup: Based on Customer Name · The app checks if the customer already exists in e-conomic by matching their name. If yes, it reuses that customer. If no, it creates a new one · Prevents duplicate customers in your accounting

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Product lookup: Based on Title · The app matches Shopify products to e-conomic products by product name · Keeps your product list consistent in both systems

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Tax handling: Automated · The app reads the tax (VAT) on each Shopify order and applies the correct tax code in e-conomic · Your VAT is booked correctly without manual work

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: To change any of these, click Customize in the top right of the settings box.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: By default, every order is sent to e-conomic as its own invoice. If you would rather book your sales as one daily summary instead of individual invoices (common for shops with many small orders), click Switch in Settings and choose Sales Summary Sync.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: This section only applies if your invoices are booked (finalized) in e-conomic. It tells the app which accounts in your chart of accounts to use when recording payments.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: When you turn on the Journal Entry Preferences toggle, a confirmation popup appears: Enable bookkeeping?

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: This popup explains that once you confirm, the app will start creating journal entries in the e-conomic accounts you select below.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Start in Manual mode. In Manual mode, the app prepares the journal entries but does not book them automatically, so you can review and test them first. Switch to Auto mode only once you have checked that the entries are correct.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Click Confirm to enable bookkeeping, or Cancel if you are not ready yet.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: If you are unsure what to choose here, click Send to accountant. This sends the settings to your accountant so they can pick the right accounts for you. You do not need to guess.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: The four fields: Clearing account for payment – a temporary "waiting" account where the payment is recorded until the money actually arrives in your bank. This keeps your bookkeeping tidy while payments are on their way.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Account for payment processor fee – the account where fees from your payment provider (for example Shopify Payments or PayPal) are recorded as a cost.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Account for payment to bank – the account that represents your bank account, where the money is recorded once it is paid out to you.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Select Journal – the journal in e-conomic where these entries are placed. A journal is simply a folder where bookkeeping entries wait for approval.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Choose an account in each dropdown and click Save.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Verify your integration before using it with live data.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: In the Quick actions box on the right, click Test with Sample Data. The app creates a test invoice in e-conomic using sample information.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Open e-conomic and confirm the test invoice appeared.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Back in the app, click Open Dashboard. The dashboard shows every order that has been synced, so you can always see what was sent to e-conomic and when.

chunks.title: Installation Steps
chunks.text: Setup is now complete. From this point on, new Shopify orders are sent to e-conomic automatically.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Set up automated journal entries for Shopify payments, fees, and payouts in e-conomic

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: The Bookkeeping page controls how your Shopify payouts, payments, and fees are recorded as journal entries in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: You find it in the app menu under Bookkeeping.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Click How bookkeeping works in the top right corner of the page for a short explanation directly inside the app.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Bookkeeping is only applicable for Booked Invoices. If your Invoice Type is set to Draft Invoice, this section does not apply.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Bookkeeping toggle Bookkeeping (Automated Bookkeeping Sync) – turns the bookkeeping sync on or off. When enabled, the app creates journal entries in e-conomic based on the preferences you set below.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Payout This setting controls how payouts are recorded in e-conomic:

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Manual – your payouts from Shopify are made available in the Cloudify Dashboard, and you push them to e-conomic manually. This lets you review each payout before it is recorded.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Auto – Cloudify automatically pushes your payout data into the e-conomic journal, with no manual step.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Start in Manual mode. Review and test your journal entries first, and switch to Auto only once you are confident the entries are correct.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: This section sets up how journal entries are added to e-conomic. Journal entries are created for:

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Shopify Payments – to record customer payments

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Shopify fees – the transaction fees Shopify charges you

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Payouts to your bank account – the money Shopify transfers to you

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Each entry goes into the journal and account you specify here. If you're unsure which accounts to pick, click Send to accountant and let your accountant choose.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Shopify processes merchant payouts cumulatively: multiple payouts are consolidated and disbursed as one scheduled transaction. The journal entries reflect this.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: The four main fields: Select Journal – the journal in e-conomic where Shopify entries are posted, for example a journal named "Webshop".

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Clearing/Contra account – the offset account for the entries, for example a Shopify clearing account. This is a temporary "waiting" account that holds amounts until the money arrives in your bank.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Payout Account (Bank A/c) – where Shopify deposits your money, most often your bank account.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Shopify Fee account – the account where Shopify transaction fees are recorded as a cost.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Three additional accounts for less common amounts in your payouts:

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Select Refund – the account for returns and refunds.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Select Reserved – the account for amounts Shopify is holding back (reserves) before paying them out.

chunks.title: Bookkeeping
chunks.text: Select Adjustment – a technical regulations account, used for small corrections and adjustments in payouts.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Control how Shopify customers are matched, numbered, and created in e-conomic

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Customer Sync Rules control how the app handles your customers: how it recognizes an existing customer in e-conomic, how customer numbers are created, what default values new customers get, and which data fields are copied over.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: You find these settings on the Sales Posting Setup page, under the Customer tab. (The Product and Invoice tabs are covered in their own guides.)

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: How do you want to match your customers?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: This setting decides how the app checks whether a Shopify customer already exists in e-conomic, so it does not create duplicates.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: You pick one field on the Shopify side and one field on the e-conomic side. The default is Customer Name on both sides: when an order comes in, the app looks for an e-conomic customer with the same name. If one exists, the invoice is attached to that customer. If not, a new customer is created.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Make sure the Shopify field you select is never empty on your orders. If the field is empty, the sync cannot match the customer and the order will trigger an error.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Use a Default Customer for Point of Sale (POS) Order – some Shopify POS orders (in-store sales) have no customer attached at all. If you tick this box, the app creates one customer in e-conomic named "POS Customer – Cloudify" and assigns all customer-less POS orders to it. Without this, those orders would fail to sync.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: How do you want to handle customer numbers?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Every customer in e-conomic has a customer number. This setting decides who creates that number when a new customer record is made:

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Let e-conomic create customer number (default) – e-conomic generates a unique number automatically. This guarantees no two customers share a number in your e-conomic account.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Take the number from Shopify – the app uses a number from a Shopify field instead. Only choose this if you already manage customer numbers in Shopify and know they are unique.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Which Shopify customer field do you want to use for e-conomic customer number?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: If e-conomic generates the customer number, you can choose to save that number back into a Shopify field, so you can see it in Shopify too.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Choose Do not add it anywhere if you do not need the number in Shopify. Nothing is written back.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: When the app creates a new customer in e-conomic, some fields are required by e-conomic but do not exist in Shopify. This section sets the default values those new customers get.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Select Payment Terms – the standard payment deadline on invoices for these customers, for example "Netto 8 dage" (payment due within 8 days).

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Select Customer Groups – the e-conomic customer group that new customers are placed in. Groups are used in e-conomic to organize customers for reporting.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Select Currency – the default currency for transactions with these customers, for example Danske kroner.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Select Invoice Layout – the invoice design/template e-conomic uses when generating invoices for these customers.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: In which country is your e-conomic account registered? – your home country. The app uses this to work out which sales are domestic and which are foreign for VAT purposes. It can be changed later under Advanced if needed.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: VAT zone mode VAT zones decide which VAT treatment a customer gets based on where they are located.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Standard Dynamic VAT Zones (default) – the app automatically assigns the VAT zone from the customer's location: Domestic, EU, or Abroad (outside the EU). For most shops this is the right choice and needs no further setup.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Advanced Country-Specific VAT Zones – choose this if certain countries need a special VAT zone that differs from the standard logic. A Country-specific settings box appears where you select a country from the dropdown and set its VAT zone. All countries you do not add continue to use the standard logic.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Customer Field Mappings This table controls which Shopify customer data is copied into which e-conomic customer field, both when a new customer is created and when an existing customer is updated.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: The most common fields are pre-mapped for you: Customer Name, Email, Phone Number, Country, City, Zip Code, and Address. You can see the state of each field in the Status column:

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Mapped (green) – this e-conomic field is filled with data from the selected Shopify field.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Not mapped (orange) – this e-conomic field is left empty. Nothing is copied.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Pick a Shopify field from the dropdown to map it.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Use Text – instead of pulling data from Shopify, type a fixed value that is used for all customers. For example, setting Credit Limit to the same amount for everyone.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Clear – remove an existing mapping so the field is left empty.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Create new Shopify field – if the data you want to map does not exist in Shopify yet, this button creates a new custom field in Shopify to hold it.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: The table has two tabs: General (the common fields) and Additional (extra fields). Use the search box to find a specific field quickly.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Fields worth knowing: Customer Name is required and cannot be cleared — e-conomic will not accept a customer without a name.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Corporate Identification Number – the company registration number, for example CVR in Denmark. Map this if you sell to businesses (B2B), since it is needed for correct invoicing.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Rules
chunks.text: Credit Limit – a maximum credit amount for the customer. Only relevant if you use credit limits in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Where to find the settings page and what it contains

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: To find the settings page, open the app in your Shopify admin and click Sales Posting Setup in the left menu.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: The Sales Posting Setup page contains everything that controls how your Shopify sales are sent to e-conomic. In short:

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Sales Posting Method – choose how transactions are recorded in e-conomic: Individual Order Mode (one invoice per Shopify order, recommended) or Sales Summary Mode (sales grouped into periodic journal entries).

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Customer tab – rules for how customers are matched between Shopify and e-conomic, how customer numbers are created, default values for new customers, VAT zones, and field mappings.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Product tab – rules for how products are matched and synced between Shopify and e-conomic.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Invoice tab – rules for how invoices are created and what they contain.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Control when invoices are created in e-conomic, their type, shipping charges, credit notes, and field mappings

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Invoice Sync Rules control when the app creates an invoice in e-conomic, whether it is a draft or booked invoice, how shipping and refunds are handled, and which order data appears on the invoice.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: You find these settings on the Sales Posting Setup page, under the Invoice tab.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Automatically create (e-conomic) Invoices

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: This setting determines when the integration creates an invoice in e-conomic, based on the status of your Shopify order. Choose one:

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: When Fulfilled (after shipping) – the invoice is created once the order has been fulfilled and shipped.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: When Paid (payment recorded in Shopify) – the invoice is created once payment is recorded on the order in Shopify.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: When Created (order created in Shopify) – the invoice is created as soon as the order is placed, regardless of payment or shipping status.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Using Shopify Flow? If you want Shopify Flow to trigger invoice creation instead — using any event you define in your Flow automation — turn this toggle off. Disabling it switches off the standard automation so it does not interfere with your Flow automation. Flow-triggered invoice creation only works when this toggle is disabled.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Choose what kind of invoice the app creates:

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Draft Invoice – the invoice is created as a draft in e-conomic. Nothing is finalized: you (or your accountant) review and book each invoice manually in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Booked Invoice – the invoice is booked (finalized) automatically in e-conomic. No manual review step.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: A booked invoice in e-conomic is final — it gets an invoice number and enters your accounts, and it cannot simply be edited or deleted afterwards. Corrections require a credit note. If you are just starting out, use Draft Invoice until you have verified that the invoices come out correctly, then switch to Booked.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Note: some features, such as Journal Entry Preferences on the Bookkeeping page, are only available for Booked Invoices.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Additional Options Include shipping charges Enable this checkbox to include the shipping charges from the Shopify order on the e-conomic invoice.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Once enabled, a dropdown appears. Select a product from the list — this product acts as the shipping line on the invoice, and the integration takes care of the shipping charges from there. The shipping amount itself always comes from the Shopify order.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: If this box is left unticked, shipping charges are not included on the e-conomic invoice.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: e-conomic Credit Notes from Shopify Refunds

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Enable this checkbox to automatically create a credit note in e-conomic when a refund is issued in Shopify. A credit note is the accounting document that reverses (fully or partly) a previously issued invoice.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Once enabled, a dropdown appears. Select a product from e-conomic to represent refunds — the actual refund amount always comes from Shopify, so the product is only a placeholder line on the credit note.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: If this box is left unticked, Shopify refunds are not sent to e-conomic, and you must create credit notes manually.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Invoice Field Mappings This section controls how Shopify order information appears on your e-conomic invoices.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: When an invoice sync runs, the system works in this order:

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: First it checks for the customer in e-conomic (and creates a new one if needed, according to your Customer Sync Rules).

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Then it checks for the products (handled according to your Product Sync Rules).

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Finally it creates the invoice with the settings on this page.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Delivery address – where the goods are delivered: Delivery Address (street), Delivery City, Delivery Date, Delivery Country, Delivery Postal Code, and Delivery Terms.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Notes and references – text and reference fields on the invoice.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: Billing address – the customer's billing address fields.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: None of these fields are mapped by default. Map them if you want the information to appear on your e-conomic invoices — for example, map the delivery address fields if you ship physical goods and want the delivery address printed on the invoice.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Rules
chunks.text: For each field you can pick a Shopify field from the dropdown, click Use Text to set one fixed value for all invoices, or Clear to remove a mapping. If the data you need does not exist in Shopify, Create new Shopify field adds a custom field to hold it. Use the search box to find a field quickly.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Control how Shopify products are matched, created, and mapped in e-conomic

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Product Sync Rules control how the app finds your products in e-conomic, what happens when a product does not exist there yet, and which product data is copied over.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: You find these settings on the Sales Posting Setup page, under the Product tab.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: When an order comes in, the app needs to find the matching product in e-conomic so it can put the right product line on the invoice. There are two ways to do this:

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Simple Search (using a specific field) – the app matches products by comparing one Shopify field to one e-conomic field. The default is Shopify Title matched against e-conomic Product Name. Select the most reliable field for identifying your products — something that is always filled out and unique to each product. If your SKUs are consistent, matching Shopify SKU against e-conomic Product Number is a strong choice.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Direct Link (map each product) – instead of matching by a field, you manually link each Shopify product to its e-conomic product one by one. This gives you full control but takes more work, and every new product must be linked before it can sync.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: This step matters for accurate invoicing and inventory. If a product cannot be found, the app falls back to the rule you choose in the next section — and the default fallback is to skip invoice generation entirely.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: This rule decides what happens when an order contains a product that the search method could not find in e-conomic:

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Skip invoice generation (default) – the integration stops for that order and no e-conomic invoice is created. This prevents errors, but you need to manually review each order with a product mismatch.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Use a default product – the invoice is created using a pre-selected e-conomic product. Only the product number of the selected default product is used for invoicing — all other details (name, price, quantity) still come from the Shopify order. This keeps the integration running, but the affected invoices may need manual review later.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Create a new product in e-conomic – the app automatically creates the missing product in e-conomic from the Shopify product details and uses it on the invoice. You select which Product Group new products are placed in (for example "Varer m/moms" – goods with VAT), which determines the sales account for new products. This ensures all products sync.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Automatic product creation may create duplicate or unnecessary products if not managed carefully — for example if the same product exists in Shopify with slightly different titles. Keep your product data clean if you use this option.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Tax settings Exclude Shopify Tax from e-conomic invoices – enable this checkbox to remove the taxes applied on the Shopify order when the e-conomic invoice is created. Only the relevant e-conomic tax is applied to the invoice instead.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Cloudify does not perform any tax calculations. The tax on the invoice depends entirely on your existing tax settings in e-conomic. This checkbox only controls whether the Shopify tax amount is carried over or left out.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Product Field Mappings This table only applies if you chose Create a new product in e-conomic above. It defines which Shopify product data is copied into which e-conomic field when a new product is created.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: The Status column shows the state of each field:

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Mapped (green) – the e-conomic field is filled from the selected Shopify field.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Not mapped (orange) – the field is left empty.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: The pre-mapped defaults: e-conomic field · Shopify field · Notes

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Product Name · Title · Required — cannot be cleared

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Product Number · SKU · Required — cannot be cleared. Make sure your Shopify products have SKUs, or product creation will fail

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Barcode · Machine-readable barcode for the product

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Product Description · Free text description

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Product Cost Price – what the product costs you. Map this if you want margin reporting in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Product Group – overrides the default product group per product, using a value from a Shopify field.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Product Recommended Price – the recommended retail price.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: For each field you can pick a Shopify field from the dropdown, click Use Text to set one fixed value for all products, or click Clear to leave the field empty. If the data you need does not exist in Shopify, Create new Shopify field adds a custom field to hold it. Use the search box to find a field quickly.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Choose how your Shopify sales are recorded in e-conomic: one invoice per order, or grouped summaries

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: The Sales Posting Method decides how your Shopify transactions are recorded in e-conomic. You find it at the top of the Sales Posting Setup page.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Click How it works in the top right corner of the page to see a short explanation of the setup directly inside the app.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: The two modes Mode · What it does · Best for

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Individual Order Mode (recommended) · Creates one e-conomic invoice for every Shopify order, with full line-item details (each product, price, and tax on the invoice) · Shops that want detailed reconciliation and a full invoice trail for every order

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Sales Summary Mode · Groups your sales into periodic summaries (for example one entry per day) and posts them as journal entries · Shops with many small orders that want to keep the e-conomic ledger clean instead of filling it with hundreds of invoices

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Switching between modes When you click the other mode, a confirmation popup appears: Change Push Method?

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: The popup warns you that switching between Individual and Summary mode changes how your future sales data is posted to e-conomic. Data that has already been pushed to e-conomic is not affected and stays as it is.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Click Confirm and Continue to switch, or Cancel to keep your current mode.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: If you choose Sales Summary Mode, a configuration page opens. Fill in the following sections and click Save.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Transfer Frequency Choose how often your sales should be grouped and sent to e-conomic:

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: The sales for the selected period are pushed to your e-conomic journal as a draft entry, meaning nothing is booked automatically — you (or your accountant) review and book the entry in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: These four fields tell the app where in e-conomic the summary entries should be recorded. If you are unsure, ask your accountant.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Journal – the journal in e-conomic where the summary entries are posted, for example a journal named "Webshop".

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Contra Account (Shopify Clearing Account) – the offset account for the entries. This is a temporary "waiting" account that holds the sales amount until the money arrives in your bank. Often called a Shopify clearing account.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Revenue Account – the account where your product sales are recorded as income.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Gift Card Liability Account – the account that holds the value of sold gift cards until the customer redeems them. Money from a sold gift card is not revenue yet — it becomes revenue when the gift card is used.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Choosing the wrong Gift Card Liability Account can cause incorrect revenue reporting. If you sell gift cards, confirm this account with your accountant.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Splitting & Grouping Split summaries by payment method – if you tick this box, the app creates a separate journal entry for each payment method you select. Payment methods you do not select are combined into one common entry. This makes it easier to reconcile each payment provider's payout against its own entry.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: When you tick the box, two new sections appear:

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Select payment methods to split – a row of payment method buttons, for example Cash, Klarna, Credit Card, Shopify Pay, PayPal, and Amazon. Click a payment method to select it. Each selected method gets its own separate journal entry.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Configure accounts per method – once you have selected one or more payment methods, this section lets you choose which e-conomic account each method posts to. This is useful because each payment provider pays out to you separately, so booking each one against its own account makes bank reconciliation much simpler. Until you select a payment method, this section shows "No payment methods selected for splitting."

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: This section controls how VAT is split in your journal entries when you sell to other countries.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: If you do not select any country: the journal entries are automatically divided into three groups based on VAT codes — Domestic, EU, and non-EU (Abroad).

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Country-Specific VAT Code: tick this box if certain countries need their own special VAT code. All other countries continue to use your standard logic above. This is relevant if you are registered for OSS (the EU scheme for reporting VAT on sales to consumers in other EU countries).

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: When you tick Country-Specific VAT Code, two settings appear:

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Business Country Selection – the country where your business is registered, for example Denmark. Sales to this country are treated as domestic.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: Country Assignments – click Add Country assignment to add a country and assign it the VAT code it should use. Repeat for each country that needs special treatment. All countries you do not add continue to follow your standard Domestic/EU/Abroad logic.

chunks.title: Sales Posting Method
chunks.text: When everything is filled in, click Save.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Customer Search Field Define how customer data is synchronized between Shopify and Fortnox. Choose a unique field, like email or VAT number, to prevent duplicates. A new customer is created only when the customer is not found in Fortnox by the defined search parameter.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Decide if Fortnox should automatically generate a customer number or if it should take the number from Shopify.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: a) Let Fortnox create the customer number

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: The customer number will be created in Fortnox. Select the Shopify field to store the Fortnox customer number or select "Do not add it anywhere" if you don’t want to store this number

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: b) Take the Fortnox customer number from Shopify

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: The customer number is taken from Shopify. Select the Shopify field, which has the customer number or select "Do not add it anywhere" if you don’t want to add this number.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Set default values for Payment Terms, Currency, Price List, Delivery Ways, Delivery Terms, VAT Types and Languages. These default values apply when new customers are created in Fortnox.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: VAT zone mode Configure VAT Zones automatically or define country-specific VAT Zones for your Fortnox customers & invoices.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Automatically assigns VAT type based on the customer’s billing country.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: The integration automatically determines your customer VAT Type based on the customer location ("SE", "Subject to EU VAT" or "Export)

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Use this if you want VAT to be fully automated across borders.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Specify a custom VAT type for selected countries.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: All other countries will still use your standard dynamic VAT logic.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Customer Field Mappings Customize the data transfer from Shopify to Fortnox to ensure accurate synchronization when a new customer is being created in Fortnox from Shopify. Some fields are mapped by default.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Click "Create new Shopify property" if you want to add any new mapping fields to the window.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Now that you've installed the app and connected your accounts, it's time to configure how information flows between Shopify and Fortnox. The quick install already covered the essential settings. With this guide, you will be able to customise your app further if needed.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Click on "Apps" and then click on "Fortnox Sync"

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Click "Settings" And you have arrived. The setup process is divided into three main areas:

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Customer Settings Product Settings Invoice Settings Each of these areas plays a crucial role in determining how your data is synchronized and how your business processes are automated.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Fulfilled-Based Creation An invoice will be created in e-conomic when the Shopify order status changes to ‘Fulfilled’. This usually means the products have been shipped. Select this option if you want to invoice customers only after their order has been dispatched.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: An invoice will be automatically created in Fortnox as soon as the Shopify order is marked as ‘Paid’. This takes place when the payment is successfully processed in Shopify, even if the products are not shipped yet, helping you maintain quicker and more accurate financial records.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Perfect for Cash-on-Delivery orders or if you’d like an invoice to be created automatically in Fortnox the moment a new order comes into your Shopify store.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Invoice Types Explained Draft Invoices Creates an editable invoice in Fortnox. You'll need to review and manually post it later. Ideal if you often need to make adjustments before finalizing invoices.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Draft Orders Creates an editable order in Fortnox. You'll need to review and manually post it later. Ideal if you often need to make adjustments before finalizing orders.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Additional Options Shipping Charges You can enable sync for shipping charges and select the corresponding charges from the product list. Fortnox doesn’t support direct sync of shipping charges, so you can add it as a product and then select it from the list to reflect the shipping charges of Shopify invoice in Fortnox.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: How should invoice data fields be mapped?

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Map the necessary fields from Shopify to Fortnox for invoice creation. You can create new fields in Shopify by clicking Create new Shopify field.

chunks.title: Products Sync Settings
chunks.text: Here, you can define your preferences based on which product sync is performed between Shopify and Fortnox.

chunks.title: Products Sync Settings
chunks.text: You have two choices when performing product sync in Fortnox:

chunks.title: Products Sync Settings
chunks.text: Note: This step is crucial for accurate invoicing and inventory management. If the product is not found, one of the options shown in the next section below is applied, where the “Skip invoice generation” option is selected by default.

chunks.title: Products Sync Settings
chunks.text: If you select "Skip invoice generation", no invoice will be generated.

chunks.title: Products Sync Settings
chunks.text: If you select Use a default product, you can select an existing product to be used for invoice generation.

chunks.title: Products Sync Settings
chunks.text: If you select Create a new product in Fortnox, a new product will be created based on the product field mapping and added to the invoice.

chunks.title: Products Sync Settings
chunks.text: Tax settings Enable this option to exclude any taxes from Shopify orders when creating Fortnox invoices. Only the relevant Fortnox tax will be applied if this option is enabled. Cloudify itself does not calculate taxes; it relies entirely on your existing tax settings in Fortnox.

chunks.title: Products Sync Settings
chunks.text: Product Field Mappings Define the field mappings from Shopify to Fortnox for invoice creation. The selected fields will be mapped. Some fields are mapped by default.

chunks.title: Products Sync Settings
chunks.text: Note: You can perform field mapping for products only if you have selected Create new product as the option for the product not found.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: This document outlines the essential prerequisites for successfully integrating Shopify and Fortnox. Adhering to these requirements will ensure a smooth integration process, optimal data synchronization, and secure operation.

chunks.title: Prerequisites

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: What you need in place before installing the Shopify-Pennylane integration.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Before integrating Shopify with Pennylane, make sure you meet the requirements below for a smooth setup.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Complete all prerequisites before starting installation. Missing any of these can block the connection partway through setup.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: *** Checklist Active Shopify store — Your store is active and you have administrative rights to install and manage apps.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Active Pennylane account — Your account is active and you have administrative privileges to connect apps and configure settings.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: The account you connect with must be allowed to authorise third-party applications in Pennylane.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: If you manage more than one company in Pennylane, confirm which company file the Shopify store should sync into before you connect.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Invoices created against the wrong company file have to be corrected manually in Pennylane. Checking this before you connect takes seconds; fixing it afterwards does not.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Have your login details for both Shopify and Pennylane ready. You'll sign in to Pennylane during setup, so you'll need access to the Pennylane account that holds the correct company and access rights.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Know how your order management, payment collection, and fulfillment work today. The integration's sync rules (when to invoice, how to match customers and products, how to handle VAT) map directly onto these processes — so a clear picture up front makes configuration faster and more accurate.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Link your Pennylane account to the app so Shopify orders can be sent to Pennylane as invoices.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Before the app can send anything to Pennylane, it needs permission to do so. This first step creates that link.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: It takes about two minutes. Nothing is synced to Pennylane yet — you are only granting access.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Connecting does not send any orders. Syncing starts only after you finish setup and turn it on.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Before you start A Pennylane account you can log in to, with permission to connect third-party apps

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Admin access to the Shopify store you want to connect

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: The app installed on that store from the Shopify App Store

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Connect your account After installing, you land on the welcome screen. Select Get started to begin setup.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: You will see the connection screen showing No account connected. Select Connect to Pennylane.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Not ready to connect yet? Select Schedule demo to book a free guided walkthrough. You can come back and finish setup at any time.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: A secure Pennylane login window opens. Sign in with your normal Pennylane credentials and confirm access when prompted.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Your Pennylane password is entered on Pennylane's own site. The app never sees or stores it.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: If you manage more than one company in Pennylane, make sure you are logged in to the correct company file before authorising. Connecting the wrong one means invoices are created in the wrong books.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: You are returned to the app, and the screen now shows Connected account with the email address used.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: The app moves on automatically after a few seconds. Select Continue to go straight to the next step, or Stay on this page if you want to review the connection first.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Opens Pennylane's login page and asks for permission to create invoices and read customer and product data on your behalf. This is what makes the whole integration work.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Appears once an account is linked. Removes the app's access to Pennylane and stops all syncing. Use it if you connected the wrong account, or if you are moving to a different Pennylane company.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Disconnecting does not delete anything already created in Pennylane.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Books a free call where our integration expert walks you through the setup and answers questions.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Common questions The login window is usually blocked by a pop-up blocker. Allow pop-ups for your Shopify admin domain and try again.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: Select Disconnect, then Connect to Pennylane again and log in with the correct account. Do this before any orders sync, so nothing lands in the wrong books.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: No. Connecting only grants access. Nothing is created in Pennylane until orders start syncing.

chunks.title: Connect Pennylane Account
chunks.text: You log in on Pennylane's own site, so the app never receives your password. Access can be revoked at any time using Disconnect, or from within Pennylane.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Set how Shopify customers are matched, created, and mapped to customer records in Pennylane.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: These settings control how the integration finds an existing customer in Pennylane, and what it fills in when it has to create a new one.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Sensible defaults are already applied. You only need to change these settings if your business works differently — for example if you sell B2B, or if you use Shopify POS.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Customer Sync Rules How do you want to match your customers?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Before creating anything, the integration looks for an existing customer in Pennylane. This setting tells it which field to compare.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: You choose a Shopify field on the left and the matching Pennylane field on the right.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Shopify field · Customer Name · The value taken from the Shopify order

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Pennylane field · Name · The Pennylane field it is compared against

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: If a match is found, the existing Pennylane customer is used. If not, a new customer is created.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Make sure the Shopify field you choose is never empty on your orders. If the field is blank, the match fails and the sync returns an error.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Names are not unique. Two different customers called "Jean Martin" will be treated as the same person. If your Pennylane records hold email addresses, matching on email is more reliable.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Use a Default Customer for Point of Sale (POS) Order

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Shopify POS orders often have no customer attached — someone walks in, pays, and leaves. Pennylane still needs a customer on the invoice.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: When this option is on, the integration creates a customer called POS Customer – Cloudify in Pennylane and assigns it to every POS order that has no customer.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Turn it on if you use Shopify POS and don't collect customer details at the till. All walk-in sales are grouped under one customer, which keeps your Pennylane contact list clean.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Turn it off if every POS sale in your store is tied to a named customer.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: How do you want to handle customer numbers?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Every customer in Pennylane has a customer number. This setting decides who generates it.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Option · When to use it Let Pennylane create customer number (default) · You want Pennylane to number customers automatically. Guarantees the number is unique across your Pennylane account.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Take customer number from Shopify · You already use your own customer reference in Shopify and want the same one in Pennylane. An existing Shopify field is used as the customer number.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: If you take the number from Shopify, you are responsible for making sure it is unique. Duplicate numbers will cause errors in Pennylane.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Which Shopify customer field do you want to use for the Pennylane customer number?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: This question follows on from the choice above, and works in one of two directions.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: If you chose "Let Pennylane create customer number", you can write the generated number back into Shopify so both systems show the same reference.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Select the Shopify field where the number should be stored, or choose Do not add it anywhere (the default) if you don't need it in Shopify.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Storing the number in Shopify makes it much easier to find the matching record in Pennylane when you're chasing a specific order.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: If you chose "Take customer number from Shopify", select the existing Shopify field that holds the reference you want to use. That value becomes the customer number in Pennylane.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Make sure the field you pick is filled in on every customer and never repeats. A blank value or a duplicate will cause the sync to fail.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: What are your default settings for new customers?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Some Pennylane fields have no equivalent in Shopify. These defaults fill them in whenever a new customer is created.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Payment Conditions · Upon receipt · The payment term applied to the customer's invoices. Shopify orders are usually already paid, so upon receipt fits most stores. Change it if you invoice B2B customers on terms such as 30 days.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Customer Type · Company · Whether new customers are created as corporate entities or individual clients. Set this to Individual if you sell mainly B2C.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Invoice Footer Template · Modèle par défaut · The footer shown at the bottom of generated invoices. The list comes from the templates in your Pennylane account.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Billing Language · French · The language used for invoices and customer communication. Change it if you invoice customers outside France.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: These defaults apply only when a customer is created. Changing them later does not update customers that already exist in Pennylane.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Customer Field Mappings How should customer data fields be mapped?

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: This is where you decide which Shopify value fills each Pennylane customer field.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Common fields are mapped for you. The mappings are grouped into four tabs:

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Name, email, phone, notes, and recipient.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Any remaining Pennylane customer fields.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Reading the table Column · What it shows Pennylane Fields · The field being filled, with a short description. Fields marked Required must have a value.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Shopify Fields · Where the value comes from. Pick a Shopify field from the dropdown, or select Use Text to enter a fixed value that is the same for every customer.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Status · Mapped means a source is set. Not mapped means the field will be left empty in Pennylane.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Action · Clear removes an existing mapping.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Required fields Three fields must be filled for a customer to be created:

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: First Name — required for individual customers

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Last Name — required for individual customers

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Company Name — required for company customers

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Which fields are required depends on the Customer Type you set in Customer Default Mappings. If you create customers as Company, Company Name must always have a value. If your Shopify orders don't reliably contain a company name, use Use Text to set a fallback, or create customers as Individual instead.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Making changes Find the Pennylane field you want to change, using the Search box if the list is long.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Open the Shopify Fields dropdown and choose a source, or select Use Text to enter a fixed value.

chunks.title: Customer Sync Settings
chunks.text: Select Save. Changes apply to customers created or updated after you save. Existing Pennylane customers are not rewritten.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Set when invoices are created in Pennylane, whether they are drafts or finalised, and how order data appears on them.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: These settings control the invoice itself — when it's created, what state it's created in, and which Shopify values appear on it.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Invoice Sync Rules Automatically create (Pennylane) Invoices

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Leave the toggle on to have invoices created automatically. Switching it off stops invoice creation entirely, while leaving your other settings in place.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Order Status This setting decides when the integration creates the invoice, based on the status of the Shopify order.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose this option to create a Pennylane invoice when the Shopify order is marked as Fulfilled. This usually happens after the order has been shipped. Use this if you want to create invoices only after products are sent to the customer.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Use this when you ship before invoicing, sell made-to-order goods, or hold stock for long periods. Cancelled orders never reach Pennylane at all.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose this option to create a Pennylane invoice as soon as the Shopify order is marked as Paid. The invoice is created after the payment is received, even if the order hasn't been shipped yet. This is a good option if you want to record sales quickly.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Use this when you offer payment methods that don't settle at checkout — bank transfer, invoice terms, cash on delivery — and you only want confirmed sales in Pennylane.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose this option to create a Pennylane invoice as soon as a new order is received in Shopify. It's ideal for Cash on Delivery (COD) orders or if you want invoices to be created immediately.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Use this when you want your books to reflect sales immediately. This suits most online stores, where payment is taken at checkout.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Only one option applies. Choose the point in your process that you'd call "the sale has happened" — your expert-comptable may have a preference here.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: This decides what state the invoice arrives in.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Option · What it means Draft Invoice (default) · The invoice is created as a draft. It can still be edited or deleted in Pennylane before it is validated.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Finalised Invoice · The invoice is issued immediately and given a number. It cannot be edited afterwards.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose Draft if you want to review invoices before they are issued. This is the safer starting point while you're checking that the integration produces what you expect.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose Finalised if you're confident in the setup and want invoices issued without a manual step.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: A finalised invoice cannot be corrected. Any mistake has to be resolved with a credit note (avoir). Test thoroughly on drafts before switching.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Credit notes from Shopify refunds only work with finalised invoices. If you leave the invoice type as Draft, the refund option below has no effect.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Additional Options Include shipping charges Enable this option to add shipping charges from the Shopify order to the Pennylane invoice. After enabling it, select any product from the list. The integration will use that product to add the shipping charge automatically.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Pennylane Credit Notes from Shopify Refunds

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: When this is on, issuing a refund in Shopify creates a credit note (avoir) in Pennylane.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: You select a Pennylane product to represent refunds. The amount comes from the Shopify refund — the product is only there to give the credit note a line to sit on.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: This works only with finalised invoices. A draft invoice has not been issued, so there is nothing to credit. If you're using drafts, edit or delete the draft in Pennylane instead.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Invoice Field Mappings How should invoice data fields be mapped?

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: This decides which Shopify values appear on the invoice.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: The customer is found in Pennylane, or created if needed.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: The products are found, following your Product Sync Rules.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: The invoice is created using the settings on this page.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: If step 1 or 2 fails, the invoice isn't created.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: The mappings are grouped into three tabs:

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Labels, references, and the invoice date.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: What appears on the invoice document itself.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: References tab Pennylane field · Default source · What it's for

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Accounting Label · Order Name · Internal accounting label for the invoice. This is what your accountant sees in the ledger.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: External Reference · Order Name · A unique reference linking the Pennylane invoice back to the Shopify order.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Date d'émission · Create Date · The invoice issue date, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Leave External Reference mapped to Order Name. It's what lets you find the Shopify order behind any invoice, and it's the first thing you'll want when something looks wrong.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: The invoice date follows the Order Status setting above. If you invoice When Created, the date is the order date; if you invoice When Paid or When Fulfilled, consider whether the create date is still the right one for your books.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Reading the table Column · What it shows Shopify Fields · Where the value comes from. Pick a field from the dropdown, or select Use Text for a fixed value.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Status · Mapped means a source is set. Not mapped means the field is left empty.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Need a value Shopify doesn't hold? Select Create new Shopify field to add one, then map it here.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Making changes Open the tab you need, and use Search if the list is long.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose a Shopify field, or select Use Text for a fixed value.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Select Save. Changes apply to invoices created after you save. Invoices already in Pennylane are not changed.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Set how Shopify products are found in Pennylane, what happens when they aren't, and how product fields are mapped.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: These settings control how the integration finds a product in Pennylane for each line on a Shopify order — and what it does when no match exists.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Getting this section right matters more than most. If a product can't be found and there's no fallback in place, the invoice isn't created at all.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Product Sync Rules Choose a product search method

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: There are two ways for the integration to find the right Pennylane product.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: The integration compares one Shopify field against one Pennylane field.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Shopify field · Title · The value taken from the Shopify order line

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Pennylane field · Designation · The Pennylane field it is compared against

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Use this when your Shopify catalogue and your Pennylane product list already share a common value — usually the product title or the SKU.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: SKU is a safer match than Title. Titles get edited for marketing reasons; SKUs usually don't.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: You map each Pennylane product to a Shopify product by hand.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Use the Search box to find a product, then pick its Shopify counterpart from the dropdown. Clear removes a mapping. The list is paginated, so work through every page.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Use this when your product names and codes don't line up between the two systems, or when you have a small, stable catalogue.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Direct Link only covers the products you map. Anything unmapped falls through to the If product not found setting below. This method needs maintaining every time you add a product.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: The first row in the list is a special option. Map a Shopify product here to put it on the invoice as a line item description only, with no Pennylane product attached.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Useful for one-off charges or items you don't want cluttering your Pennylane product list.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: This is the fallback. It decides what happens when the search above comes back empty.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: If the Shopify product isn't found, the integration will skip creating the invoice in Pennylane. This helps avoid errors, but you'll need to check and fix the missing products manually.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: One unmatched line blocks the entire invoice, not just that line.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: If the Shopify product isn't found, the integration will still create the invoice in Pennylane using the product you selected. Only the product ID comes from the selected Pennylane product. The product name, price, and quantity are taken from Shopify.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: If the Shopify product isn't found, the integration will automatically create a new product in Pennylane using the Shopify product details. Choose a product group for new products. This makes sure all products are synced, but it may create duplicate products if the same product already exists.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Two settings apply to every product created this way:

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Setting · What it does VAT Type · The VAT rate given to the new product. Set this to the rate you actually sell at — for most French merchants that is 20%.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Revenue Account (optional) · The Pennylane account the sales are posted to. Leave it blank to use your Pennylane default.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: This option can create duplicate or unnecessary products if your Shopify titles vary. Two spellings of the same product become two products in Pennylane.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Check the VAT Type before you save. Every product created by the integration inherits it, and correcting the VAT on invoices already issued means raising credit notes (avoirs).

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Tax settings Exclude Shopify Tax from Pennylane invoices

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Enable this option to remove Shopify taxes when creating invoices in Pennylane. If enabled, only the tax set in Pennylane will be applied to the invoice.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Product Field Mappings This section applies only if you chose Create a new product in Pennylane above. If you didn't, nothing here has any effect.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: How should product data fields be mapped?

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: This decides which Shopify value fills each field on a newly created Pennylane product.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Pennylane field · Default source · What it's for

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Designation (required) · Title · The product label shown on the invoice.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Description · Free-text product description.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Reference · SKU · Your product reference or SKU.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Product Identification · SKU · A unique external reference used to match the product on later syncs.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: HT Price · Unit price excluding VAT. HT stands for hors taxes.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Unit · Not mapped · Unit of measure on the invoice line — each, hour, kg.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Currency · Not mapped · Three-letter currency code. Defaults to EUR when left empty.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: VAT · Not mapped · Pennylane VAT rate code, for example FR_200 for 20%. Overrides the default VAT rate set above.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Revenue Account · Not mapped · The Pennylane revenue account for this product. Overrides the default set above.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Reading the table Column · What it shows Shopify Fields · Where the value comes from. Pick a field from the dropdown, or select Use Text to enter the same fixed value for every product.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Status · Mapped means a source is set. Not mapped means the field is left empty and Pennylane's own default applies.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Leaving VAT and Revenue Account unmapped is fine for most stores — the defaults you set under Create a new product in Pennylane are used instead. Map them only if different products need different rates or accounts.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: HT Price must be the price before VAT. If your Shopify prices include VAT, mapping them straight into this field will overstate your revenue. Check with your expert-comptable if you're unsure which way your store is configured.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Making changes Find the Pennylane field, using the Search box if the list is long.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Choose a Shopify field from the dropdown, or select Use Text for a fixed value.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Select Save. Mappings apply to products created after you save. Products already in Pennylane are not changed.

chunks.title: Customer Sync settings
chunks.text: Customer Match Rule Define how customers are matched between Shopify and Tripletex. Select a Shopify field and the Tripletex field it should be matched against. The integration uses this pairing to check whether a customer already exists in Tripletex — a new customer is created only when no match is found, which prevents duplicates.

chunks.title: Customer Sync settings
chunks.text: Where possible, match on a field that is unique per customer to keep duplicates out.

chunks.title: Customer Sync settings
chunks.text: Ensure the selected Shopify field is not empty on your orders. An empty match field will trigger sync errors.

chunks.title: Customer Sync settings
chunks.text: Default Customer for POS Orders (Optional) — Enable Use a Default Customer for Point of Sale (POS) Orders if you process in-person sales. When a Shopify POS order doesn't have a customer assigned, the integration automatically creates a customer named POS Customer – Cloudify in Tripletex and uses it for all POS invoices where no customer information is available.

chunks.title: Customer Sync settings
chunks.text: *** How Should Customer Data Fields Be Mapped?

chunks.title: Customer Sync settings
chunks.text: Specify how Shopify customer data maps to Tripletex fields. This controls how customer information is transferred when a customer is created or updated in Tripletex. Some common fields — such as Name and Telephone — are pre-mapped for you.

chunks.title: Customer Sync settings
chunks.text: To change a mapped field, click its box and select your preferred Shopify field.

chunks.title: Customer Sync settings
chunks.text: To map a fixed value instead of a Shopify field, click Use Text and enter the value.

chunks.title: Customer Sync settings
chunks.text: Click Create new Shopify field to add a mapping that isn't listed.

chunks.title: Customer Sync settings
chunks.text: Fields are grouped across tabs — General, Postal address, Invoice settings, Business address, Delivery address, and Additional. The Status column shows whether each field is Mapped or Not mapped.

chunks.title: Customer Sync settings
chunks.text: Name is required. Map all relevant customer fields before going live to avoid incomplete customer records being created in Tripletex.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Now that you've installed the app and connected your accounts, it's time to configure how information flows between Shopify and Tripletex. The quick install already covered the essential settings. With this guide, you will be able to customise your app further if needed.

chunks.title: Getting Started
