chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Setup process The setup process is divided into three main areas:

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Customer Settings Product Settings Invoice Settings Each of these areas plays a crucial role in determining how your data is synchronized and how your business processes are automated.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: These settings control when an invoice is created in Tripletex, what form it takes, and which extra details (shipping, refunds) carry across from Shopify.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: This decides the point in the Shopify order's life at which the integration creates the invoice in Tripletex.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: When Fulfilled (after shipping) — The invoice is created once the Shopify order is marked Fulfilled, i.e. after you've shipped. Choose this if you only want to invoice orders that have actually gone out.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: When Paid (payment recorded in Shopify) — The invoice is created as soon as Shopify records the order as Paid, whether or not it has shipped. Choose this for faster financial record-keeping.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: When Created (order created in Shopify) (default)* — The invoice is created the moment a new order lands in Shopify. Suits Cash-on-Delivery (COD) orders, or any case where you want the record in Tripletex right away.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: This sets what the integration creates in Tripletex for each order.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Draft Invoice — Creates an editable draft invoice. Nothing is finalized — you review and post it in Tripletex yourself. Choose this if you usually adjust invoices before they go out.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Draft Order — Creates a draft order rather than an invoice. Choose this when your workflow starts from an order in Tripletex (for example, so you can pick, confirm, or invoice it there on your own schedule).

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Additional Options Optional settings that control how extra order details carry into Tripletex. Each option reveals a dropdown when enabled, so you can tell the integration exactly how to handle it.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Include shipping charges — Carries the Shopify shipping cost onto the Tripletex invoice so it appears correctly. When enabled, use the dropdown to choose how shipping is represented in Tripletex.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Tripletex Credit Notes from Shopify Refunds — Creates a credit note in Tripletex whenever a Shopify order is refunded, keeping refunds reflected in your accounting. When enabled, use the dropdown to configure how refunds are handled in Tripletex.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Configure these settings to streamline shipping charges, credit note creation from Shopify refunds, and automated invoice emails to your customers.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** How Should Invoice Data Fields Be Mapped?

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Set how Shopify order information appears on your Tripletex invoices. For each Tripletex field, choose the Shopify field it should pull from, use Use Text to enter a fixed value, or click Clear to remove a mapping. Add fields that aren't listed with Create new Shopify field. Click Save when done.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: When an invoice sync runs, the integration works in this order:

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Checks for the customer in Tripletex (and creates one if needed)

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Checks for the products (handled by your Product Sync Rules)

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Creates the invoice with the settings above

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Fields are grouped across the Order, General, and Invoice tabs, and the Status column shows whether each is Mapped or Not mapped.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Order tab fields Tripletex Field · Description

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Delivery Address Line 1 · Line 1 of the order delivery address.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Delivery Address Line 2 · Line 2 of the order delivery address.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Delivery Address City · City of the order delivery address.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Delivery Address Country · Country of the order delivery address.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Order Date · Order date, in \YYYY-MM-DD\ format. Defaults to today if not mapped.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Delivery Date · Delivery date, in \YYYY-MM-DD\ format. Required by the Tripletex API — defaults to today if not mapped.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Comment to customer · Comment printed on the invoice generated from this order.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Packing note · Delivery comment on the order.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: The General and Invoice tabs contain additional fields you can map the same way.

chunks.title: Invoice Sync Settings
chunks.text: Delivery date defaults to today if left unmapped. Map it to the correct Shopify field if your Tripletex workflow depends on accurate delivery dates.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: These settings control how the integration matches Shopify products to products in Tripletex when building an invoice, and what happens when no match is found.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: When a Shopify order syncs, the integration needs to find the matching product in Tripletex before it can add it to an invoice. Pick how that lookup works:

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Simple Search (using a specific field) — Match on a single field. Choose the Shopify field (e.g. Title) and the Tripletex field it should be matched against (e.g. Name). The integration looks for a Tripletex product where that field matches.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Direct Link (no searching) — Manually link each Shopify product to a specific Tripletex product. No lookup runs — the integration uses the link you set. Best for smaller catalogs where you want exact control over which product maps to which.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Why it matters: this step drives accurate invoicing and inventory. If a product can't be found, the integration falls back to your setting in If product not found in Tripletex below — where Skip invoice generation is applied by default.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: This decides what happens when the search above returns no match. Pick one:

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Skip invoice generation (default)* — The invoice is not created. Use this when you'd rather catch and fix a missing product than let an incomplete invoice through.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Use a default product — The order still invoices, but the unmatched line uses an existing Tripletex product you nominate as the fallback.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Create a new product in Tripletex — A new product is created from your product field mappings and added to the invoice. You'll need to select a sales account for the new products.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: *** Tax Settings Enable Exclude Shopify Tax from Tripletex invoices to drop the tax that came in on the Shopify order. When enabled, only the relevant Tripletex tax is applied to the invoice.

chunks.title: Product Sync Settings
chunks.text: Cloudify does not calculate tax itself — the amount applied depends entirely on your existing tax configuration in Tripletex.

chunks.text: *** Search, Filter & Sort Search — Click the search icon to search across all orders.

chunks.title: Cloudify Dashboard
chunks.text: Add filter — Filter the list by Payment status or Fulfillment status.

chunks.text: Sort — Sort by Date, Order Number, Customer Name, Payment Status, Fulfillment Status, or Total, in either Oldest to newest or Newest to oldest order.

chunks.title: Cloudify Dashboard
chunks.text: Re Run — For an order whose Sync status is Failed, fix the underlying issue first, then click Re Run to retry.

chunks.title: Cloudify Dashboard
chunks.text: *** Sync Information Click the View (eye) icon on any order to open its Sync Information. This shows the result of the last sync — a success confirmation, or the specific reason a sync failed and what to change.

chunks.title: Cloudify Dashboard
chunks.text: For example, if an order failed because the product wasn't found in Tripletex and your product preference is set to Skip invoice generation, the message tells you to either choose a default product or enable search-and-create in your Product Sync settings, then re-run.

chunks.title: Cloudify Dashboard
chunks.text: If a sync fails, always open Sync Information first — it names the exact cause, so you know whether to fix a mapping, a product setting, or the connection before hitting Re Run.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Before integrating Shopify with Tripletex, make sure you meet the requirements below for a smooth setup.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Complete all prerequisites before starting installation. Missing any of these can block the connection partway through setup.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: *** Checklist Active Shopify store — Your store is active and you have administrative rights to install and manage apps.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Active Tripletex account — Your account is active and you have administrative privileges to connect apps and configure settings.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: The integration module (API access) must be activated in Tripletex before you can generate an API token. Without it, the connection cannot be completed.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: If the integration module isn't active, you won't be able to generate a token — and setup will stall at the connection step. Activate it in Tripletex first.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Have your login details for both Shopify and Tripletex ready. You'll generate a Tripletex API token during setup, so you'll need access to the Tripletex account that holds the correct company and access rights.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Know how your order management, payment collection, and fulfillment work today. The integration's sync rules (when to invoice, how to match customers and products, how to handle tax) map directly onto these processes — so a clear picture up front makes configuration faster and more accurate.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Follow the steps below to install the app, generate your Tripletex API token, and connect your account to Shopify.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: *** Installation Open Shopify-Tripletex by Cloudify from the Shopify App Store, select Install, and click "Let's Get Started" to authorize the installation.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Click "Connect to Tripletex". You'll be prompted to enter your Tripletex API token.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Before generating a token, note the following:

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: The integration module must be activated in Tripletex before you can generate a token. Without that module, the connection process cannot continue.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Need help? Click "See how to generate your API token" for a step-by-step walkthrough.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Log in to Tripletex — If needed, switch to the correct company by clicking the company name in the header.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Open the employee record — Go to Company → Employees in the left menu. Open the employee whose access rights will be used for this integration.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Open API access — Inside the employee record, go to API access and click New token.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Configure the token — Select Adapted setup and All entitlements. Enter the application name, then enter a token name and click Create token.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Copy the token — Copy the generated token and click OK.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Store the token securely as soon as it is created. Tripletex will not show it again.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Once you have the token, paste it into the token field in the app and click Connect.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Make sure you are connecting with the token from the correct Tripletex company account. Administrative privileges are required to complete this step.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Once the token connects successfully, you'll land on the final setup screen confirming everything is configured and ready.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Test with Sample Data — Run a demo sync with sample data to see how a Shopify order flows into Tripletex before going live.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account
chunks.text: Open Dashboard — Go live with your real orders. Your first real sync activates automation, and every future order is handled automatically.

chunks.title: Connect Tripletex Account

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Welcome to the Shopify-Xero Integration Setup Guide. This comprehensive resource will guide you through the process of connecting your Shopify and Xero accounts, enabling seamless data synchronization and workflow automation between these powerful platforms.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Integration Benefits By integrating Shopify with Xero, your organization can:

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Automate invoice creation directly in Xero for every Shopify order

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Seamlessly synchronize customer and product data across both platforms

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Eliminate manual data entry, minimizing errors and saving valuable time

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Daily sales summaries posted to Xero for fast bookkeeping and reconciliation

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: One unified dashboard to track every invoice, refund, payout, and sync error

chunks.title: Overview

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The table below shows what data is synced between Shopify and Xero. The data flow is unidirectional from Shopify to Xero except for the invoice number synced back into Shopify order notes.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Before integrating Shopify with Xero, you need to ensure that you meet several key requirements to enable a smooth and effective setup. Here is a concise checklist:

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Account Access Active Shopify Store: Make sure your Shopify store is active with full administrative rights to manage apps and integrations.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Active Xero Account: Confirm that your Xero account is active and that you have administrative privileges to connect apps and configure settings.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Credentials Ready: Gather your login information for both Shopify and Xero. These are very crucial for secure authentication during integration.

chunks.title: Prerequisites
chunks.text: Business Processes: Have a foundational understanding of your order management, payment collection, fulfillment, inventory processes, and reporting needs. This insight will help you configure the integration effectively and ensure data flows match your actual business operations.

chunks.title: Connect your account

chunks.title: Connect your account

chunks.title: Connect your account
chunks.text: Instant invoices — Automatic Xero invoice creation for every Shopify order.

chunks.title: Connect your account
chunks.text: Accurate sync — Customer and tax data stays consistent across platforms.

chunks.title: Connect your account
chunks.text: Save time — Save up to 5 minutes of manual entry per order.

chunks.title: Connect your account
chunks.text: *** Step 2 — Connect to Xero Connect your Xero account to authorize the integration with Shopify.

chunks.title: Connect your account
chunks.text: Click "Connect to Xero" and sign in with your Xero credentials. Once authorized, the integration will have access to create invoices, contacts, and items in your Xero org.

chunks.title: Connect your account

chunks.title: Connect your account

chunks.title: Connect your account

chunks.title: Connect your account

chunks.title: Connect your account
chunks.text: Combine all transactions into a single consolidated invoice and credit note each day.

chunks.title: Connect your account
chunks.text: Keep your bank ledger tidy. Recommended for high-volume stores.

chunks.title: Product Sync
chunks.text: Select Search Parameters Set Custom Mappings Use this option when you want to connect products manually between Stripe and e-conomic.

chunks.title: Product Sync
chunks.text: This works well for smaller inventories where you want tighter control over which Stripe product maps to which e-conomic product.

chunks.title: Product Sync
chunks.text: Matching similar field types usually gives the best results. For example, SKU to Product Number is often a strong choice.

chunks.title: Product Sync
chunks.text: Choose this option if you want the integration to stop when a matching product is not found.

chunks.text: This is useful when you want to review mismatches manually before anything is created.

chunks.title: Product Sync

chunks.title: Connect Visma e-conomic Account
chunks.text: Are you ready to supercharge your webshop to accounting workflow? Our simple process seamlessly connects your Stripe and e-conomic accounts, bringing powerful synchronisation to your fingertips. This integration allows you to effortlessly manage your webshop data and make invoices/orders all from within your familiar Stripe interface.

chunks.title: Invoice Rules
chunks.text: Configure when invoices or orders should be created in e-conomic based on the Stripe invoice stage.

chunks.title: Invoice Rules
chunks.text: Use these settings to control when the integration should create an invoice or order in e-conomic based on the Stripe invoice stage.

chunks.title: Invoice Rules
chunks.text: Invoice Generation Rules First, choose when the integration should trigger invoice or order creation in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Invoice Rules
chunks.text: You can choose one of these Stripe stages:

chunks.title: Invoice Rules

chunks.title: Invoice Rules
chunks.text: Create Draft Invoice Booked Invoice Draft Order Invoice Rules Invoice Or Order Types Create Draft Invoice Creates an editable invoice in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Invoice Rules
chunks.text: Use this when you want to review or adjust the invoice manually before finalizing it.

chunks.title: Invoice Rules
chunks.text: Draft Order Creates an editable order in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Invoice Rules

chunks.title: Invoice Rules
chunks.text: Use this when your billing process is standardized and manual review is not usually required.

chunks.title: Invoice Rules

chunks.title: Invoice Rules

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: Configure how Stripe products are matched to e-conomic products and choose what should happen when a product is not found.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: Use these settings to control how Stripe products are matched with e-conomic products during invoice creation.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: Product Matching Method Choose your preferred product matching approach.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: Simple Search Use Simple Search when you want to match products using a specific field such as Name or SKU.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: This option lets you define matching rules and use product data consistently across both systems.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: Direct Link Use Direct Link when you want to manually connect Stripe products to e-conomic products one-to-one.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: This option is ideal for smaller product catalogues where you want more precise control over each mapping.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: You can only use one product search method at a time: Simple Search or Direct Link.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: Under Advanced settings, choose what should happen when a Stripe product is not found in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: Skip Invoice Generation Choose this option if you do not want an invoice to be created when the matching product cannot be found.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: This helps prevent incorrect invoices and keeps product accounting more controlled, but it may require manual intervention.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: Skip Invoice Generation Use A Default Product Choose this option if you want to replace the missing product with a predefined product in e-conomic.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: The integration will use the product number from the selected default product, while the other line-item details such as name, quantity, and price will still come from Stripe.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: Use A Default Product Create A New Product In e-conomic

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: Choose this option if you want the integration to automatically create a new product in e-conomic based on the Stripe product.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: You also need to choose the product group that should be used for newly created products.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: You can enable invoice-level discounts even though e-conomic only supports product-level discounts.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: When enabled, the integration adds the overall discount as a line item so the discount information is reflected correctly in both Stripe and e-conomic.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: You can also create a payment for your customers without sending any product.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: To do this, select the product SKU that should be used for reference purposes, then click Finish.

chunks.title: Product Rules
chunks.text: You can always change these settings later if your business needs change.

chunks.title: Contact Settings

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Setting up the Stripe to Microsoft Business Central Integration

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Now that you've installed the app and connected your accounts, it's time to configure how information flows between Stripe and Microsoft Business Central. With this guide, you will be able to customise your app further if needed.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Click "Sync Setup" And you have arrived. The setup process is divided into two main areas:

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Contact Setting Invoice Settings Each of these areas plays a crucial role in determining how your data is synchronized and how your business processes are automated.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: Configure how Stripe invoice data is matched, when invoices should be created in Business Central, and how invoice fields should be mapped.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: Use these settings to control how Stripe invoice data should be handled before an invoice is created in Business Central.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: Invoice Sync Rules Product Matching Method Choose how products from Stripe should be identified and matched in Business Central during invoice creation.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: Select Search Parameters Use this option when you want to match products by comparing a Stripe field with a Business Central field.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: SKU To Product Number Metadata Fields To Matching Business Central Fields

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: You can also use Stripe metadata fields as search parameters. Select Metadata from Stripe, then enter the metadata field name exactly as it appears in Stripe.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: Select Search Parameters Set Custom Mappings Use this option when you want to manually link specific Stripe products to specific Business Central products.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: This is especially useful when you have a smaller product catalogue and want tighter control over exact product matching.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: Set Custom Mappings Choose only one matching method at a time: Select Search Parameters or Set Custom Mappings.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: Choose what should happen if a product from Stripe cannot be found in Business Central.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: Do Not Generate Invoice Choose this option if you want the integration to stop invoice creation when a matching product cannot be found.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: This helps ensure that only complete and accurate invoices are created.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: Do Not Generate Invoice Use Default Product Choose this option if you want the integration to use a predefined Business Central product when the Stripe product cannot be found.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: The default product is used to provide the product reference, while the remaining invoice information still comes from Stripe.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: Use Default Product Invoice Trigger Stage Choose the invoice stage in Stripe that should trigger invoice creation in Business Central.

chunks.title: Invoice Settings
chunks.text: The page notes that this can be tied to different points in the Stripe invoice lifecycle, such as when an invoice is first issued, updated, or paid. It also notes that invoices in Business Central will be created in Open status. :contentReference\[oaicite:1]

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Welcome to the Stripe-Business Central Integration Setup Guide. This comprehensive resource will help you connect your Stripe and Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central accounts, enabling seamless data synchronization and workflow automation between these powerful platforms.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Integration Benefits By integrating Stripe with Business Central, your organization can:

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Automate invoice generation from Stripe payments

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Maintain synchronized customer data across both platforms

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Keep financial records aligned automatically

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Eliminate manual data entry and reduce errors

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The setup process consists of four main stages:

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Getting Started: Initial setup and account connection

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Customer Settings: Configure customer data synchronization

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Product Settings: Set up product catalog matching

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Invoice/Order Settings: Define invoice and order creation and management rules

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Prerequisites Before beginning the integration process, please ensure you have:

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: An active Stripe account with administrative access

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: An active Business Central account with administrative access

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Necessary authentication credentials for both platforms

chunks.title: Choose Your Subscription Plans
chunks.text: You'll arrive at the subscription screen. Here, you can select your preferred plan. The trial plan, which comes with 15 free credits, is selected by default. Once you've chosen your plan, proceed to the next step.

chunks.title: Choose Your Subscription Plans
chunks.text: After choosing your subscription plan, you’ll be redirected to the Settings page , where you can configure your sync settings.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Connect your Stripe account with Business Central and streamline your accounting workflow. Easily sync your Stripe data, reduce manual work, and keep your financial records organized and up to date.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Search Cloudify Business Central in Stripe Marketplace

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Click on the 'Install App' button. You'll be redirected to the Stripe app page.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Install App button Complete the authorization process for Stripe. Click "Install app"

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Connect your Business Central account when prompted. Click "Connect Business Central"

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Select the Environment for your Business Central account.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Select the Company within that environment, then click "Save" to continue.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: To sync with Stripe, you'll first need to upload and deploy the extension in your Business Central account. Download the extension package file from here.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: In Dynamics 365 Business Central (make sure you're logged into the same Company and Environment selected in the previous window), use search to open the Extension Management page.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Click on Manage, then click "Upload Extension"

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Click the three dots near Select .app file and upload the extension file you downloaded.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Toggle on "By deploying this extension you accept..." — this step is important and required before you can deploy.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Click "Deploy" to upload and deploy the extension.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Use search to open Extension Installation Status and confirm the extension has finished installing.

chunks.title: Connect Business Central account
chunks.text: Once it’s installed, click Next. You’ll be taken to the Subscription page, where you can select the available plan based on your business needs.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: *** The Chat Bubble — Available on Every Page

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: You don't need to be on the Support page to get help. The blue circular chat button sits in the bottom-right corner of every page in Lighthouse — on Overview, Billing, Workflow Runs, Connections, and everywhere else.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: Click it at any time to open the AI assistant panel. You'll see suggested prompts to get started quickly — for example:

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: Quick answers about your subscription and billing options — without raising a ticket.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: Jump directly to billing configuration guidance — useful when you're already on the Billing page and need help.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: You can also type freely in the Ask AI... input for any question about the platform.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: The chat bubble is your fastest route to help — use it for quick questions on any page before raising a formal ticket. If the AI can't resolve your issue, it will guide you to generate a support ticket for Cloudify.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: A workflow run that fails repeatedly after replaying

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: A connection that appears to have broken

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: A workflow that isn't triggering when expected

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: A data error in the destination app that you can't resolve in the source app

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: A request to modify or expand an existing workflow

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: A single failed run where the source data issue is clear (fix in your app → Replay)

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: A missing field in a source app record (fill it in → Replay)

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: A run showing as Pending (wait for it to process — this is usually temporary)

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: A question about what a workflow does (refer to the Workflows page description)

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: Before raising a ticket for a failed workflow run, always try the Replay first after fixing the source data. Most single failures resolve this way without needing Cloudify's involvement.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: *** What Happens After You Raise a Ticket

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: Your ticket is logged in the Cloudify system and appears in your Support page immediately with Open status.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: A Cloudify engineer reviews your ticket and begins investigation. The status updates to In Progress.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: Cloudify resolves the issue — whether that's a code fix, a connection repair, or a configuration change — and communicates the outcome to you.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: Once resolved and confirmed, the ticket moves to Closed status and remains in your history for reference.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: In the Support page, look for the option to create a new ticket (button or form). Provide a clear description of the issue, the affected workflow or connection, and any relevant run IDs from the Workflow Runs page. The more context you include, the faster Cloudify can resolve it.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: Response times vary by plan and issue severity. Critical issues affecting live integrations are prioritised. Contact your Cloudify account manager if you need information about your specific SLA.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: Yes. Open the ticket and add a comment or update. Always include the run ID from Workflow Runs if the issue relates to a specific failed execution — this helps Cloudify investigate immediately.

chunks.title: Support
chunks.text: For critical issues, contact your Cloudify account manager directly. The Support ticket system is for standard requests. Urgent issues affecting live data flows should be escalated through your primary contact at Cloudify.

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: View active members, manage pending invitations, and invite new people to your Lighthouse organisation.

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: The Members page is where you manage who has access to your Lighthouse account. View current team members, change their roles, remove access, manage pending invitations, and invite new people to your organisation.

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: *** Active Members The Active Members section lists everyone currently in your organisation.

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: Each member row shows: Element · Description Name · The member's display name

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: Role · A dropdown showing their current role — click to change it

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: Remove · Red button — removes this member from the organisation immediately

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: Clicking Remove immediately revokes the member's access to Lighthouse. This cannot be undone from within the platform — the user would need to be re-invited. Only remove a member when you are certain access should be revoked.

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: *** Roles and Permissions Every member is assigned one of three roles. Roles control what each person can see and do inside Lighthouse.

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: Role · Access Level Owner · Full administrative access — can manage members, billing, connections, workflows, and all platform settings

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: Editor · Can view and edit workflows and connections — cannot manage members, billing, or organisation-level settings

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: Viewer · Read-only access — can view workflow runs, connections, and dashboards, but cannot make any changes

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: Role assignments can be changed at any time from the Active Members list. Click the role dropdown on any member row and select the new role. The change takes effect immediately.

chunks.title: Members
chunks.text: Assign Viewer to team members who only need to monitor integration activity — for example, a manager reviewing run counts or a finance contact checking billing. Reserve Editor for team members actively working with workflows and connections. Limit Owner to administrators responsible for the account.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Welcome to the WooCommerce–Xero setup guide.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Welcome to the WooCommerce–Xero setup guide. This plugin helps you connect your WooCommerce store with Xero accounting software so order, customer, and product data can move efficiently between the two systems.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Integration Benefits By integrating WooCommerce with Xero, your organisation can:

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Automatically convert WooCommerce orders into Xero invoices or quotes

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Find or create customer records in Xero based on incoming order data

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Find or create product records in Xero based on items in each order

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: Reduce time spent on manual data entry between your store and your accounts

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text: The data flow is one-way, from WooCommerce to Xero.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: The Customer section has three tabs: Customer Sync Rules, Customer Default Mappings, and Customer Field Mappings. Work through each tab and click Save before moving to the next.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: *** Customer Sync Rules When an order is placed in WooCommerce, the integration searches for the matching customer in Xero before creating an invoice. This tab tells it how to do that search.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: You select one field from WooCommerce and one field from Xero. The integration compares the two values — if they match, the existing Xero contact is used. If no match is found, a new contact is created automatically.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Why this matters: If the integration cannot reliably identify your customers, it will create duplicate contacts in Xero. Duplicate contacts lead to messy records, reconciliation issues, and inaccurate invoicing history.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Which field to choose: Email address is the most reliable option. It is unique per customer and almost always filled in on a WooCommerce order. Fields like first name are not unique — two customers named "John" will cause a mismatch.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: The WooCommerce field you select must not be empty on orders. If the field is blank, the integration cannot search for a match and will trigger an error.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: When the integration creates a new customer in Xero, Xero assigns that contact a unique ID. This setting controls two things: who generates the ID, and whether it is stored back in WooCommerce.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Let Xero create the contact ID is the recommended option. Xero auto-generates a unique identifier and you can optionally select a WooCommerce field to save it in. Storing the Xero contact ID in WooCommerce makes future matching faster and more reliable.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: If you do not need to store it, select Do not add it anywhere.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: This tab sets the default values applied when the integration creates a new customer record in Xero. These defaults fill in required Xero fields that may not exist on a WooCommerce customer record.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Why this matters: Xero requires certain fields to be populated when creating a contact — for example, currency and tax rate. If these are left unconfigured, new customer records may be created with incorrect or missing accounting information, which causes problems when processing payments or filing tax returns.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Set each field to match your Xero account configuration:

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Setting · What to set Currency · The currency your store trades in

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Sales default amounts · Whether your prices are tax inclusive or exclusive — match your Xero pricing setup

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Branding theme · The invoice or quote template applied in Xero

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Invoice due date · How many days after the invoice date payment is expected

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Sales tax · The tax rate that applies to your sales

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Sales account · The Xero account code where sales revenue is recorded

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: *** Customer Field Mappings This tab controls exactly which WooCommerce customer fields are transferred to Xero when a new contact is created. Each row maps one Xero contact field to a WooCommerce field.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Why this matters: The more accurately your customer data is mapped, the less manual correction is needed in Xero. Incomplete mappings mean your Xero contacts may be missing names, addresses, or contact details — making it harder to send invoices.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Fields are organised into four groups: General, Billing Address, Delivery Address, and Additional.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Contact Name is mandatory and must be mapped. Without it, Xero cannot create a valid contact record. Some fields are pre-mapped by default — you can edit or delete any mapping to suit your requirements.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Fields showing Not Mapped will not be transferred to Xero. To add a mapping, click Edit next to the relevant Xero field and select the corresponding WooCommerce field.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: How to access the integration settings in your WordPress admin panel.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Step 1: Open the Plugin From the WordPress admin sidebar, open Sync Orders with Xero – Cloudify, or simply hover over the plugin and click Settings.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: The plugin dashboard shows three sections: Xero Connection, Integration Settings, and Subscription.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Click Open Settings under Integration Settings.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: *** Overview of Settings The Integration Settings page gives an overview of the three configuration areas:

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Customer Mapping — Match WooCommerce customers to existing Xero contacts or create new ones automatically on each order.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Product Mapping — Map WooCommerce products to Xero inventory items, or have new items created automatically on first sync.

chunks.title: Getting Started
chunks.text: Invoice & Quote Settings — Choose whether WooCommerce orders sync as Xero invoices or quotes, and configure default accounts and tax rates.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: The Invoices/Quotes section has two tabs: Invoice/Quote Sync Rules and Invoice/Quote Field Mappings. Work through each tab and click Save before moving to the next.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: This tab defines the trigger for creating invoice/quote in Xero and what type of document is created. Getting these settings right ensures your Xero records accurately reflect what was sold, to whom, and when.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Order Stage This setting answers the question: at what point in the WooCommerce order lifecycle should Xero be notified?

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: The order stage you select is the trigger. When a WooCommerce order reaches that stage, the integration creates a document in Xero.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Stage · Meaning Pending Payment · Order received, payment not yet confirmed

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Processing · Payment confirmed, order being prepared

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: On Hold · Awaiting manual review or payment confirmation

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Cancelled · Order cancelled by customer or admin

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Draft · Order saved but not yet submitted

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Completed is the recommended default for most stores — it ensures an invoice is only created once the order is fully fulfilled, keeping your accounts clean and avoiding invoices for orders that may still be cancelled or refunded.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: If your accounting process requires earlier visibility — for example, recording revenue at the point of payment — Processing may be more appropriate.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Document Type Choose whether the integration creates a draft invoice or a quote in Xero.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Draft invoice — Use for confirmed sales. A draft invoice records the transaction as a receivable in Xero and can be approved and sent to the customer directly from Xero.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Quote — Use when an order is not yet confirmed or when you need to send an estimate before committing to the sale.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Most WooCommerce stores should use Create draft invoice. Quotes are more relevant if you use WooCommerce to collect enquiries or provisional orders.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Shipping Fees By default, shipping costs are not included as a separate line item on Xero invoices. Enabling this option adds shipping as a distinct line item, linked to a specific Xero product.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: To enable it: Check Select a default item to add line item for Shipping Fee.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: A product dropdown will appear. Select the Xero item that represents your shipping charge.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: This tab controls which WooCommerce order fields are transferred to Xero invoice fields. These mappings populate the header-level details of the invoice — the dates, reference numbers, and currency — rather than the line items.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Why this matters: Accurate invoice metadata makes reconciliation easier. Mapping the invoice number or order reference means you can cross-reference Xero invoices back to WooCommerce orders without manual searching.

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Issue Date · Order Created Date · Pre-mapped — uses the date the order was placed

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Due Date · Not Mapped · Must use YYYY-MM-DD format if mapped

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Invoice Number · Not Mapped · Map this to keep Xero invoice numbers in sync with WooCommerce order numbers

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Reference · Not Mapped · Useful for adding an internal order reference to the Xero invoice

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Currency Code · Not Mapped · Provide the currency code only (e.g. USD, GBP, AUD)

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: Add to Item Description · Not Mapped · Appends additional WooCommerce data to the Xero line item description

chunks.title: Invoice/Quote Search Rules
chunks.text: To update a mapping, click Edit next to the relevant Xero field and select the corresponding WooCommerce field. Fields showing Not Mapped will not be populated in Xero unless a mapping is added.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: The Products section has two tabs: Product Sync Rules and Product Field Mappings. Work through each tab and click Save before moving to the next.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: *** Product Sync Rules When an order syncs from WooCommerce, the integration searches Xero for a matching product to build the invoice line items correctly. This tab controls how that search works and what happens when a product cannot be found.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Select Search Parameters This method automatically searches Xero for a product by comparing a WooCommerce field against a Xero field each time an order syncs. No manual work is required after the initial setup.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: This is the right choice for most stores. Matching by SKU to Product Code is the most reliable approach — SKUs are unique identifiers and rarely change. Matching by Product Name is less reliable because names can vary in formatting between platforms.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Set Custom Mappings This method lets you manually link each WooCommerce product to a specific Xero item, one by one. It is best suited to stores with a small, stable product catalogue where you want complete control over which Xero item is used for each WooCommerce product.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: You can only use one search method at a time. Switching methods will replace your previous configuration.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: This setting determines what happens when no matching product can be found in Xero. Configure this deliberately — the wrong default can result in missing invoices or unwanted products being created in your Xero account.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Do not generate invoice · The invoice is skipped entirely · When every product must exist in Xero before invoicing

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Use a default item · A fallback Xero item is used in place of the missing product · When you want invoices to always generate but can review line items later

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Create a new item · A new Xero item is created automatically from WooCommerce product data · When your WooCommerce catalogue is the source of truth and you want Xero to mirror it

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Create a new item is the most hands-off option, but it can produce duplicate or unnecessary items in Xero if product names vary slightly between orders. Review your Xero item list periodically if you use this option.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: *** Product Field Mappings This tab controls which WooCommerce product fields are transferred to Xero when a new item is created. Each row maps one Xero item field to a WooCommerce product field.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Why this matters: When the integration creates a new product in Xero, it uses these mappings to populate the item record. Incomplete or incorrect mappings result in Xero items with missing names, codes, or prices — which creates reconciliation issues and makes your Xero item list harder to manage.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Name · Product Name · Pre-mapped — required

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Code · Product SKU · Pre-mapped — required

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Description · Product Description · Pre-mapped

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Sale price · Product Sales Price · Pre-mapped

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Purchase Description · Not Mapped · Internal purchase notes

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Cost price · Not Mapped · Purchase cost of the item

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: Item Name and Code are mandatory fields and must be mapped. Without them, Xero cannot create a valid item record.

chunks.title: Product Search Rules
chunks.text: To update a mapping, click Edit next to the relevant Xero field and select the corresponding WooCommerce field. Fields showing Not Mapped will not be populated in Xero unless a mapping is added.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: When an order syncs from WooCommerce, the integration needs to find the right customer in Xero before it can create an invoice. This step tells it how to do that search.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Customer Matching You select one field from WooCommerce and one field from Xero. The integration compares the two values on every sync — if they match, the existing Xero contact is used. If no match is found, a new contact is created automatically.

chunks.title: Customer Search Rules
chunks.text: Email address is the most reliable option. It is unique to each customer and almost always filled in on a WooCommerce order. Matching by first name, for example, risks incorrect matches when two customers share the same name.

chunks.title: Invoice / Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Configure when and how WooCommerce orders are converted into Xero invoices or quotes.

chunks.title: Invoice / Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: This step controls when the integration creates a document in Xero and what type of document it creates. These are the most important settings in the setup — they determine how your WooCommerce sales appear in your Xero account.

chunks.title: Invoice / Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Order Stage The order stage is the trigger. When a WooCommerce order reaches the status you select here, the integration automatically creates a document in Xero.

chunks.title: Invoice / Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Completed is the recommended default for most stores. It ensures a document is only created once the order has been fully fulfilled — keeping your Xero records clean and avoiding invoices for orders that might still be cancelled or refunded.

chunks.title: Invoice / Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: If your business needs to record revenue earlier — for example, at the point of payment — you can select Processing instead.

chunks.title: Invoice / Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Document Type Choose whether the integration creates a draft invoice or a quote in Xero.

chunks.title: Invoice / Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Draft invoice — The right choice for most stores. It records the sale as a receivable in Xero, which you can approve and send to your customer directly from Xero.

chunks.title: Invoice / Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Quote — Use this if your WooCommerce orders represent estimates or pending sales that haven't been confirmed yet.

chunks.title: Invoice / Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: Shipping Fees If you charge shipping on your orders, you can include it as a separate line item on your Xero invoices.

chunks.title: Invoice / Quote Creation Rules
chunks.text: If you leave this disabled, shipping costs will not appear as a line item in Xero.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Configure how WooCommerce products are matched to items in Xero.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: When an order syncs, the integration needs to match each WooCommerce product to an item in Xero to build the invoice line items correctly. This step controls how that matching works.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Product Matching Simple Search — The integration automatically searches Xero for a product by comparing a WooCommerce field against a Xero field on every sync. This is the right choice for most stores.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Matching by SKU to Product Code gives the most reliable results — SKUs are unique identifiers that rarely change. Matching by product name is less reliable as names can vary slightly between platforms.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Direct Link — You manually link each WooCommerce product to a Xero item, one by one. This works well for stores with a small, stable product catalogue where you want precise control over the matching.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: This setting decides what happens when the integration cannot find a matching product in Xero.

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Option · What happens Skip invoice generation · The invoice is skipped if the product is not found

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Use a default item · A predefined fallback item is used in place of the missing product

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Create a new item · A new product is automatically created in Xero using the WooCommerce product details

chunks.title: Product Sync Rules
chunks.text: Create a new item is the most convenient option but can generate duplicate products in Xero if your product names or SKUs are inconsistent. Review your Xero item list periodically if you use this option.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Track every integration execution — inspect run details, understand failures, and replay runs directly from the Lighthouse dashboard.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: The Workflow Runs page is your real-time log of every integration execution inside Lighthouse. Every time a connected app sends an event — a new HubSpot deal, an updated contact, a completed order — Lighthouse creates a workflow run record that you can inspect, filter, and replay.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Use this page to answer three core questions:

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: If something went wrong — which step failed and why?

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Can I replay a run without waiting for the next trigger?

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: *** Reading the Runs List Each row in the table represents a single workflow execution.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Column · What It Shows Reference · The source record that triggered the run — e.g. HubSpot Deal ID: 49649660024

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: ID · The unique numeric identifier for this run — e.g. 33222. Always include this in support requests

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Workflow · The integration that executed — e.g. HubSpot → Xero Invoice

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Status · The run outcome: Finished, Failed, Running, or Pending

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Started · The date and time the run began executing

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: *** Run Status Reference Status · Meaning · What To Do

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Finished · All steps completed successfully · No action needed. Review details if you want to verify outputs

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Failed · One or more steps encountered an error and the run could not complete · Click Explain for a summary. Click View to inspect the failed step. Retrigger after fixing the root cause

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Running · The workflow is currently in progress · Wait for it to complete. Refresh the page to see the updated status

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Pending · The run is queued and waiting to start · No action needed — it will start automatically

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Skipped · The run was intentionally skipped based on your workflow logic · No action needed. Skipped runs are expected — the workflow evaluated the event and determined no action was required

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: *** Row Controls Every row has three interactive controls on the right-hand side. Together they give you full visibility and recovery capability without leaving the page.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Generates a plain-English AI summary of the run — what happened, which step failed, and likely cause. Use this first before reading technical logs.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Click the eye icon Opens the full Workflow Run detail page — event payload, step-by-step execution log, duration, and the Re-run button.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Click the three-dot menu Dropdown with two options: Retrigger (replay the run) and View (same as the eye icon).

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: *** 💬 The Explain Button Clicking the speech-bubble icon on any row generates an AI-powered plain-English explanation of that run — no JSON reading required.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Use Explain first on any failed run. It will tell you which step failed, why it failed, and whether you need to fix something in your source system before retriggering.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: The specific reason for the failure (e.g. a missing required field, an API authentication error, or a duplicate record check)

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Whether the failure is likely to resolve on retrigger or requires a data fix first

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: The Explain button is also available on the individual Run Detail page, positioned alongside the step logs so you can read both together.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: *** 👁 The Run Detail Page Clicking the eye icon — or selecting View from the Actions menu — opens the full detail view for that run.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Run Metadata Header The top section shows everything you need to know about the run at a glance.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: ID · The unique run identifier. Include this in any support request

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Workflow · The name of the integration that was executed

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Status · Final run state: finished, failed, running, or pending

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: HubSpot Deal ID · The source record that triggered this run

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Mode · Live (production data) or Test (sandbox). Shown as a green or grey badge

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Duration · Total time taken to complete all steps

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Created · When the run record was first created in Lighthouse

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Started · When Lighthouse began executing the workflow steps

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Finished · When the final step completed (or failed)

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Attempts · How many times Lighthouse attempted this run — useful for identifying retry loops

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: The Re-run Button The blue Re-run button in the top-right replays the run using the original stored event payload.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Re-run uses the data captured at the time of the original run. If the source record in HubSpot has been updated since then, Re-run will execute using the old data — not the current values. Use Retrigger from the Actions menu if you want to re-fetch the latest record from the source system.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: The Event Block identifies what triggered this run:

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Event ID — the internal ID of the incoming event that caused the workflow to start

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Type — the event category (e.g. other, contact.created, deal.propertyChange)

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Click to view details — expands the raw event payload panel on the right, showing the full JSON data Lighthouse received from the source app

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: The Steps section shows each action inside your workflow in sequence.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Element · What It Shows Step number · Steps run in order from top to bottom — Step 1, Step 2, Step 3...

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Key · The internal name of the step — e.g. fetch-deal-details, find-or-create-xero-contact

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Status · Whether this individual step finished, failed, or is still running

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Finished · The exact time this step completed

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Click to view details · Expands inline to show the step's input data, output data, and any error message

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: When a run fails, scroll through the Steps list to find the first step with a red status — that is where the problem occurred. Expand it using Click to view details to read the error message and the data that was passed into that step. This almost always reveals the root cause.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Event Details Panel The right-hand panel shows the raw JSON payload of the selected event or step — the exact data Lighthouse received from or sent to the connected system. Use this panel to:

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Verify that the correct HubSpot deal properties were captured

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Check that field values match what your destination app (e.g. Xero) requires

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Copy the payload to share with the Cloudify support team

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: *** The Actions Menu Click the three-dot menu on any row to access two actions: Retrigger and View.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Use Retrigger when... · Use Re-run when...

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: The source record in HubSpot has been updated since the original run · You want to replay the exact data that was captured at the time of the original run

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: You fixed a data issue and want the workflow to pick up the corrected values · The failure was a transient error (e.g. a timeout) with no data changes needed

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: You want to test whether a configuration change resolves the issue with current data · You want to confirm the original payload now processes correctly after a Cloudify fix

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Retriggering a run that already succeeded will create a second execution. For workflows that create records in Xero or other destination systems, this may produce duplicate entries. Always confirm the original run failed or produced incorrect output before retriggering.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Click View in the top-right corner of the Workflow Runs list to open the Toggle columns panel. Use it to show or hide columns based on what you need.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Column · What It Shows · When to Enable It

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Id · The unique run ID · Always — useful for referencing runs in support

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: WorkflowName · The name of the integration · Always — essential when running multiple workflows

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: WorkflowId · The internal workflow definition ID · Only when debugging with Cloudify support

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Status · The run outcome · Always — core to daily monitoring

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: StartedAt · When the run began · Always — sort by this to see the most recent runs first

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: CreatedAt · When the run record was created in Lighthouse · Optional — differs from StartedAt only for queued runs

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Mode · Live or Test execution context · Enable when running tests alongside live workflows

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Recommended default: Enable Id, WorkflowName, Status, and StartedAt. Add Mode during active testing to clearly separate sandbox runs from production runs in the list.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: *** Filtering Runs Use the filter bar at the top of the list to narrow down what you see.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Filter · Use It To Search box · Search by reference (e.g. a HubSpot Deal ID) or by run ID — useful when a client reports an issue with a specific record

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Pick a date · Filter by a specific date or date range — use this to investigate incidents from a particular day

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Status · Show only runs with a specific status — Pending, Running, Finished, Failed, or Skipped. Set to Failed to surface all current issues at once

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Workflow · Filter by integration name — useful when multiple workflows are active and you want to isolate one

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Mode · Filter by Live or Test — separates production runs from sandbox runs during setup and testing

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Click 💬 Explain (speech-bubble icon) on the row for a plain-English summary.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Click 👁 View (eye icon) to open the detail page.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: In the Steps section, find the first step with a red status.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Expand it using Click to view details to read the error message.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Fix the root cause in the source system (e.g. HubSpot), then use ⋯ → Retrigger.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Use ⋯ → Retrigger from the Actions menu. This re-fetches the latest record from HubSpot and runs the workflow from scratch using the updated data. Do not use Re-run — it replays the original (now outdated) payload.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Open the detail page using 👁 View and click the blue Re-run button. This replays the original event payload without re-fetching from HubSpot — correct when the data was fine but the execution failed transiently.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: In the filter bar, set Status to Failed and click Pick a date to select the relevant date. The list will show only failed runs from that day.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Open the detail page using 👁 View. In the Steps section, find the step that writes to Xero (e.g. create-xero-invoice). Expand it using Click to view details. The right-hand Event Details panel shows the exact output data that was sent.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Open the detail page and note the Run ID from the metadata header. In the Event Details panel, copy the relevant payload using the copy icon. Include both the Run ID and the payload in your support ticket — this lets Cloudify investigate immediately without additional back-and-forth.

chunks.title: Workflow Runs
chunks.text: Pending means the run is queued and waiting for Lighthouse to start processing it. This is typically temporary — refresh the page after a few moments. If a run stays Pending for an extended period, raise a support ticket.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: View all integration workflows built for your account — check deployment status, review descriptions, and manage workflows directly from the dashboard.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: *** Reading a Workflow Card Element · What It Shows Name · The workflow name — e.g. HubSpot Closed Won → Xero Invoice

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: ID · The unique internal ID — e.g. ID: 1496. Use this in support requests

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Dev / Live · Deployment status — see below

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: AI badge · Shown when the workflow uses AI-assisted logic

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Toggle · Shows whether the workflow is enabled (blue) or paused (grey)

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Description · A plain-English summary of what the workflow does and when it triggers

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: By · The Cloudify team member who built or last edited this workflow

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Updated · When the workflow was last modified

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Every workflow has a coloured status badge in the top-right of its card.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: The workflow is active and processing real data. Events from your connected apps will trigger this workflow automatically.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: The workflow is in development or testing mode. It is not processing live data yet. Cloudify will move it to Live once it has been tested and approved.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: You do not need to change workflow status yourself. The Cloudify team manages the promotion from Dev to Live as part of your integration delivery.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: *** The Three-Dot Menu Click the ⋯ menu on any workflow card to access management options.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Activates a paused workflow so it begins processing events again.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Opens a read-only view of the full workflow configuration.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Opens the workflow editor. Contact Cloudify before making any edits — changes to live workflows affect real data.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Shows the webhook URL used to trigger this workflow. See below for details.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Permanently removes the workflow. This cannot be undone.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Do not delete or edit a Live workflow without consulting Cloudify first. Changes to live workflows immediately affect your running integrations and may cause data errors.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: *** Viewing Trigger URLs Selecting Triggers from the ⋯ menu opens a modal showing the webhook endpoint for that workflow.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Element · What It Shows Environment · Dev or Live — matches the workflow's current deployment status

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Webhook URL · The endpoint Lighthouse listens on for incoming events for this workflow

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Copy icon · Click to copy the URL to your clipboard

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Toggle · Enables or disables this specific trigger endpoint

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Trigger URLs are managed by Cloudify and pre-configured as part of your integration setup. You typically only need to view this if you are troubleshooting a webhook connection with your source system.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Click Request new Workflow in the top-right corner to submit a request to the Cloudify team.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: When requesting a new workflow, include as much detail as possible about the trigger condition, the source app, the destination app, and the expected outcome. The more context you provide, the faster Cloudify can scope and build it.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: *** Searching Workflows Use the Search for your workflows field to find a workflow by name — useful when you have a large number of integrations deployed.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: Dev workflows are in development or testing — they do not process real data. Live workflows are active and handling real events from your connected apps. Cloudify promotes workflows from Dev to Live after testing and sign-off.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: A grey toggle means the workflow is paused. It will not process any events until re-enabled. If you did not intentionally pause it, contact Cloudify to investigate.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: The AI badge indicates the workflow uses AI-assisted logic — for example, intelligent data mapping or conditional routing. These workflows are built and managed by Cloudify.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: You can access the editor via ⋯ → Edit, but we strongly recommend contacting Cloudify before making any changes to a Live workflow. Incorrect edits can break running integrations and cause data issues in your connected apps.

chunks.title: Workflows
chunks.text: A trigger URL is a webhook endpoint that your source system uses to notify Lighthouse when an event occurs. These are pre-configured by Cloudify — you only need to view them if you are troubleshooting why a workflow isn't firing.
